established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. - {"content": "# Contributing\n\nThis repository expects small, test-backed changes with matching documentation updates.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.10 or newer for local linting\n- Docker with Compose current for the containerized Odoo test runner\n- Git Bash, WSL, or another POSIX shell for the `ci/*.sh` scripts on Windows\n\n## Local setup\n\n```bash\ncp ci/.env.example ci/.env\npython -m pip install --upgrade pip\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\nKeep `ci/.env` local-only. Integration keys can be copied from `ci/integrations.env.example` or provided by your shell environment.\n\n## Focused test commands\n\nRun targeted suites for the main maintained flows:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite portal_public_ops\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite finance_reporting\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite rosters_readiness_guard\n```\n\nRun an individual module when you only need a narrow slice:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_result_control\n```\n\nList the named suites from the runner itself:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n## Pre-push checks\n\nBefore release qualification, commit or intentionally discard all tracked\nchanges and remove generated runtime configuration. The RC preflight enforces\nthat the candidate can be reproduced from its commit:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh preflight\n```\n\nRun the normal development checks afterward:\n\n```bash\nblack --check sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nflake8 sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nbash -n ci/run_tests.sh\nbash -n ci/apply_env_to_ir_config.sh\nbash -n ci/restore_backup_drill.sh\npython3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py\npython3 ci/check_markdown_links.py\npython3 ci/check_module_owners.py\npython3 ci/check_openapi_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_release_train.py\npython3 ci/check_explain_snapshots.py\npython3 ci/check_ci_hygiene.py\npython3 ci/check_workflow_state_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_module_dependency_drift.py\nbash ci/prune_ci_logs.sh 30\n```\n\n## CI/CD Pipeline\n\n### Named test suites\n\nThe CI runner groups modules into named suites for focused feedback. Use the\nsuite that covers the area you changed:\n\n| Suite | Modules covered |\n|---|---|\n| `competition_core` | Base, tournament, scheduling, results, standings critical path |\n| `portal_public_ops` | Portal ownership, public routes, compliance, standings, venue-facing flows |\n| `finance_reporting` | Finance bridge and reporting coverage |\n| `rosters_readiness_guard` | Participant readiness regression and discovery gate |\n| `release_surfaces` | Broader portal/public, match-day, compliance, notification release verification |\n| `people_rosters_rules` | People, rosters, rules, and officiating modules |\n| `ops_and_notifications` | Discipline, governance, notifications, import_tools, demo modules |\n\n```bash\n# Run a named suite\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Run a single module (fastest for narrow changes)\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings\n\n# Run everything (use before merging)\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh\n\n# List suites\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n### Reading CI output\n\nThe runner prints a results block at the end:\n\n```\n════════════════════════════════\n  RESULTS\n════════════════════════════════\n  Exit code:     0\n  Tests run:     62\n  Tests passed:  62\n  Tests failed:  0\n  Test errors:   0\n════════════════════════════════\n```\n\nA non-zero exit code means failure. Find the cause:\n\n```bash\n# Show failing test names and tracebacks\ndocker logs <container> 2>&1 | grep -A 20 \"FAIL\\|ERROR\\|Traceback\"\n```\n\nThe container name is printed by `docker compose ps` or appears in the runner\noutput as `sf_ci-ci-odoo-run-<hash>`.\n\n### CI gate stages\n\n1. **Module install** — all declared modules install without error.\n2. **Test run** — `TransactionCase` and `HttpCase` tests execute.\n3. **Query-count checks** — `assertQueryCount` assertions verify no N+1\n   regressions were introduced.\n4. **EXPLAIN snapshots** — `ci/check_explain_snapshots.py` compares query\n   plans against stored baselines.\n5. **Doc freshness checks** — `ci/check_doc_freshness.py`, `check_markdown_links.py`,\n   `check_module_owners.py`, `check_openapi_contracts.py` verify documentation\n   and contracts are up to date.\n6. **Workflow contract checks** — `ci/check_workflow_state_contracts.py` verifies\n   that documented lifecycle states and required workflow actions stay aligned\n   with model declarations.\n\n### Workflow contract map upkeep\n\n- Keep `_workflows/contracts/workflow_state_contracts.json` aligned with each\n  canonical workflow markdown and model state source.\n- If CI reports undocumented states, either add the state to the matching\n  workflow markdown and contract entry or remove/rename the code state.\n- If CI reports missing actions, add the action method in code with the\n  expected guardrails or update the contract when the workflow changed by design.\n\n### Iterating on a failing test\n\n```bash\n# 1. Make your code change\n# 2. Run only the affected module\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_<name>\n# 3. If it passes, run the full suite before pushing\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite <suite>\n```\n\nKeep the `--keep` flag to leave the Docker stack running between iterations\n(avoids paying the container startup cost each run):\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings --keep\n# ... fix code ...\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings --keep\n```\n\nUse `--keep-on-failure` for automatic cleanup on success and retained\ncontainers/database/filestore/configuration on failure. For fast UI work use\n`--frontend-module`; for cross-module safety use\n`--affected-from origin/main --include-dependents`. Workspace contracts can be\ncombined with:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_competition_contracts\n```\n\n### Pre-push checks\n\nBefore pushing, run the static checks locally to avoid a CI round-trip:\n\n```bash\nblack --check sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament \\\n      sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues \\\n      sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nflake8 sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament \\\n       sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues \\\n       sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nbash -n ci/run_tests.sh\npython3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py\npython3 ci/check_markdown_links.py\npython3 ci/check_module_owners.py\npython3 ci/check_openapi_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_release_train.py\npython3 ci/check_explain_snapshots.py\npython3 ci/check_module_dependency_drift.py\npython3 ci/check_migration_review.py\npython3 ci/check_constraint_index_contracts.py\n```\n\n## Documentation expectations\n\n- Update the relevant module README for behavior or schema changes.\n- Update the matching workflow under `_workflows/` when business behavior changes.\n- Keep `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md`, and `STATE_AND_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md` aligned when the change affects their scope.\n- Update `MODULE_OWNERS.yaml` whenever a new addon is introduced or primary module ownership changes.\n- Update `DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md` when a change modifies cleanup scope or retention windows for logs, staged deliveries, or generated report files.\n- Update the relevant record under `adr/` when a change revises portal trust boundaries, reporting SQL-view policy, or public route ownership.\n\n## Module implementation checklist\n\nWhen adding an addon or persistent model, keep the change complete and\ninstallable:\n\n- Declare direct dependencies and every XML/CSV file in `__manifest__.py`.\n- Export model, wizard, and controller packages from their `__init__.py` files.\n- Add ACLs and record rules for every new model; check company and portal scope.\n- Add a module README, focused regression test, and workflow update when the\n  change introduces a business state or user journey.\n- For a new module, use the standard layout: `models/`, `security/`, `views/`,\n  optional `data/`, `wizards/`, `controllers/`, and `tests/`. Do not create\n  empty directories.\n\n## Migration review checklist\n\nFor model, view, controller, security, or ownership changes, record the\naffected modules and release train, then verify:\n\n- schema, backfill, index, view, route, and ACL implications are understood;\n- `python3 ci/check_migration_review.py --base-ref origin/main` passes;\n- the migration dry-run command and result are recorded in\n  `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md`;\n- rollback triggers, backup requirements, and any SQL reversal are recorded in\n  the same runbook;\n- the affected module tests and the relevant full suite pass.\n\n## Architecture summary\n\nThe dependency direction is `base → tournament → competition_core → registration → format → calendar → scheduling`, followed\nby domain modules such as people, rules, rosters, officiating, results,\nstandings, compliance, discipline, governance, venues, and finance. Portal,\npublic-site, notification, reporting, and import modules are integration or\nsurface layers. A module may import only from declared dependencies; use the\nmodule README and manifest as the final authority.\n", "content_length": 9387, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "CONTRIBUTING.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "579e6cbb224f72795e722ae5881989da3962e71d5dd6771d5d7985bff96c1c00", "size_bytes": 9603}

Cleanup Result |\n|---------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|----------------|\n| Notification logs | `pending` | 30 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `sent` | 90 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Notification logs | `failed` | 180 days | `create_date` | Delete old log row |\n| Inbound deliveries | `cancelled` | 90 days | | `processed_with_errors` | 180 days | `processed_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Inbound deliveries | `failed` | 365 days | `received_on` | Delete delivery and staged payload attachment |\n| Generated report files | Last successful export snapshot | 60 days | `last_run_on` | Clear stored file payload and filename, keep schedule |\n\n## Automation\n\nThe cleanup routines run through daily scheduled actions that ship with the\naffected addons:\n\n- `sports_federation_notifications.ir_cron_notification_log_retention`\n- remain visible in the operator checklist.\n- Report schedule retention clears the stored export artifact but preserves the\n  schedule definition, run metadata, and next execution date.\n- If audit, legal, or incident-response requirements require a longer window,\n  update the model retention constants and this document in the same branch.\n\n## Change Management\n\nWhen retention windows or cleanup scope change:\n\n1. Evidence is read-only to federation managers and is retained independently from the records cleaned by the policy.\n\n\n## Recovery visibility\n\nFederation managers use **Administration → Retention and Recovery** to verify policy freshness and outcomes. --{"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. -+{"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Competition Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Competition Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. If a target date\npasses without a removal decision, extend it here with the reason.\n\n- Slug-based public routes are canonical.\n- Numeric public routes remain compatibility shims and should not be used for\n  new integrations.\n- The `/api/v1/competitions` routes are canonical. Any numeric-ID aliases remain\n  deprecated compatibility surfaces and must not be used for new integrations.\n- Older CSV shapes should remain available for one supported release cycle once\n  a replacement contract is published.\n- Removals must be announced by updating this file, relevant READMEs, and the\n  roadmap in the same release window.\n\n## Integration configuration\n\nCI and local development use environment variables for SMTP, OAuth, partner\ntokens, webhooks, and object storage. Copy `ci/integrations.env.example` to\n`ci/.env`; never commit credentials. The CI helper writes non-empty values to\nOdoo system parameters with the `integration.` prefix, including:\n\n- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_USE_TLS`,\n  `EMAIL_FROM`;\n- `SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `MAILGUN_API_KEY`;\n- `OAUTH_GOOGLE_*`, `OAUTH_GITHUB_*`;\n- `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`;\n- `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_REGION`;\n- `ALLOWED_HOSTS`.\n\nRead global parameters through `ir.config_parameter` and do not log secret\nvalues. Upload malware scanning, when enabled, uses\n`sports_federation.attachment_scan.command` and\n`sports_federation.attachment_scan.timeout_seconds`; exit code `0` means clean,\n`10` means infected, and any other non-zero code means verification failed.\n\n## Notification matrix\n\nThe notification dispatcher is non-blocking and records delivery outcomes in\n`federation.notification.log`. Business actions trigger the following current\nnotifications:\n\n| Event | Recipient or audience | Channel |\n|---|---|---|\n| Season registration confirmed or returned | Submitting representative or club contact | Email |\n| Tournament published | Participant club and team contacts | Email |\n| Participant confirmed | Team and club contacts | Email |\n| Result submitted | Result validators | Activity |\n| Result approved or contested | Team/club contacts; managers for contests | Email |\n| Standing frozen | Participant club contacts | Email |\n| Finance event confirmed | Partner or club/player/referee contact | Email |\n| Referee assigned | Referee | Email |\n| Overdue referee confirmation or officiating shortage | Federation managers | Activity |\n\nDelivery failures must not roll back the business transaction. Failed sends are\nlogged for retry or operator investigation; dispatcher methods must not raise a\nbusiness validation error.\n\n\n## Public competition feed v1\n\n`GET /api/v1/competitions` and `GET /api/v1/competitions/<edition_slug>` expose only published, non-sensitive competition data. It stores:\n\n- `modules.txt` with the exact install/upgrade module list\n- `<db>_<timestamp>.dump` as a PostgreSQL custom-format dump\n- `filestore_<db>_<timestamp>.tar.gz` when a filestore exists under\n  `./odoo-data/filestore/<db>`\n\nDo not use `--skip-backup` for production releases.\n\nRun the periodic restore drill against one of these backup directories before\nor during each release train using the restore checklist in this runbook:\n\n```bash\nbash addons/ci/restore_backup_drill.sh --backup-dir 2026-04-15_191410 --target-db odoo_restore_drill --dry-run\n```\n\n## Production Upgrade\n\nRun the upgrade and let the script restart the live Odoo service afterward so\nPython changes are loaded by the running web container:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/upgrade_sports_federation.sh --db odoo\n```\n\nFor a non-interactive upgrade that excludes demo data, use `--yes`. To include\nthe demo addon non-interactively, add `--install-demo`.\n\nThe script installs modules that are missing or uninstalled, upgrades modules\nthat are already installed, and restarts the Odoo service. It runs:\n\n- `odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <db> -i <install_module_csv> -u <upgrade_module_csv> --stop-after-init`\n- `docker compose restart odoo`\n\nThe demo addon is excluded by default. Open **Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners**.\n2. Filter for partners where **Token Rotation Required** is checked, or where\n   **Last Rotated On** is older than the rotation policy window.\n3. The wizard reveals the new raw token **once** (it cannot be retrieved again).\n   Copy it immediately and deliver it to the partner over a secure channel\n   (not email in plain text).\n5. The `token_rotation_required` flag clears automatically after a successful\n   rotation.\n\n**After a migration from plaintext storage:**\n\nIf `sports_federation_import_tools` was upgraded from a version prior to\n`19.0.1.2.0`, existing plaintext tokens were hashed in place and flagged for\nrotation by the post-migration script. Partners with `Token Rotation Required`\nset to `True` are still functional (their hashed token verifies correctly)\nbut should be rotated and re-issued at the next opportunity.\n\n**Verification:**\n\nAfter rotation, ask the partner to make one authenticated test call and confirm\na `200 OK` response to `/integration/v1/contracts`. A `401` response with\n`access_denied` indicates the token was not delivered correctly.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the upgrade must be rolled back:\n\n1. Open **Federation > Import Tools > Integration Partners**.\n2. Filter for partners where **Token Rotation Required** is checked, or where\n   **Last Rotated On** is older than the rotation policy window.\n3. The wizard reveals the new raw token **once** (it cannot be retrieved again).\n   Copy it immediately and deliver it to the partner over a secure channel\n   (not email in plain text).\n5. The `token_rotation_required` flag clears automatically after a successful\n   rotation.\n\n**After a migration from plaintext storage:**\n\nIf `sports_federation_import_tools` was upgraded from a version prior to\n`19.0.1.2.0`, existing plaintext tokens were hashed in place and flagged for\nrotation by the post-migration script. - {"content": "# Workflow: Discipline Pipeline\n\nFrom match incident through review, decision, sanctions, suspensions, and case\nclosure.\n\n## Overview\n\nWhen an incident occurs during or around a match, federation staff capture it\nas a **match incident**, group related facts into a **disciplinary case**, and\nthen record sanctions or suspensions as outcomes. The workflow is intentionally\nauditable: incidents stay linked to the case, cases carry dated decisions, and\nfinancial penalties flow into the finance bridge when enabled.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Incidents, cases, sanctions, suspensions |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Match context where incidents occur |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player subject records |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referee as incident reporter |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Club subject records |\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Fine amounts as finance events |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Appeals or exceptional follow-up |\n| `mail` | Chatter on discipline records |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Incident Reporting\n\n**Actor**: Referee, match official, or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_discipline`\n\n1. During or after a match, create a **match incident** record.\n2. Fill in the match context and at least one subject reference:\n   - match\n   - player\n   - club\n   - reporting referee\n3. Choose an incident type such as `warning`, `yellow_card`, `red_card`,\n   `misconduct`, `violence`, `admin_issue`, or `other`.\n4. Add the minute and a factual description.\n5. The incident is created in `new` status.\n6. `date_reported` and `reported_by_user_id` are recorded automatically.\n\nIncidents are visible from the match form and remain standalone until they are\nattached to a case.\n\n### 2. Case Drafting\n\n**Actor**: Disciplinary staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_discipline`\n\n1. Create a **disciplinary case** to group one or more related incidents.\n2. The case receives an automatic reference number via `ir.sequence`\n   (`FED-DISC-XXXXX`).\n3. Link the relevant incident records.\n4. Identify the subject: player, club, or referee.\n5. Assign a responsible user if the review has a named case owner.\n6. The case starts in `draft`.\n\n### 3. Review\n\n**Actor**: Case handler or disciplinary staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_discipline`\n\n1. Submit the case for review: `draft` → `under_review`.\n2. Linked incidents that were still `new` are marked `attached`.\n3. Review the evidence: incident notes, match sheet, referee report, and any\n   supporting material.\n4. If the case was submitted too early or needs corrections, use **Reopen** to\n   return it from `under_review` to `draft`.\n\nThe reopen path is only available while the case is under review. It is a\ncorrection step, not a post-decision appeal mechanism.\n\n### 4. Decision\n\n**Actor**: Disciplinary committee or case handler\n**Module**: `sports_federation_discipline`\n\n1. Once the review is complete, decide the case: `under_review` → `decided`.\n2. `decided_on` is recorded automatically.\n3. Create one or more **sanctions** and/or **suspensions** as outcomes.\n\n#### Sanctions\n\n| Type | Description |\n|------|-------------|\n| `fine` | Monetary penalty |\n| `warning` | Formal warning |\n| `ban` | Competition ban |\n| `point_deduction` | Standing penalty |\n| `other` | Custom disciplinary outcome |\n\nEach sanction records the target, effective date, and optional amount.\n\n#### Suspensions\n\nA suspension is a time-bound match ban for a player.\n\n- `date_start` / `date_end` define the ban window.\n- States: `draft` → `active` → `expired` / `cancelled`.\n- Active suspensions are consumed by match-sheet eligibility checks.\n\n### 5. Financial Recording\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_finance_bridge`\n\n1. When a sanction of type `fine` is created, the finance bridge can create a\n   linked **finance event**.\n2. The finance event keeps the sanction traceability through source fields.\n3. Finance events follow their own lifecycle: `draft` → `confirmed` → `settled`\n   or `cancelled`.\n\n### 6. Appeal Or Exceptional Follow-Up\n\n**Actor**: Sanctioned party, federation governance staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. If the decision is disputed, open an **override request** through the\n   governance workflow.\n2. Mark the case as `appealed` when the disciplinary record needs to show that\n   the original decision is under formal challenge.\n3. Governance outcomes may lead to operational follow-up outside the case, but\n   the case remains the canonical history of the disciplinary review itself.\n\n### 7. Case Closure\n\n**Actor**: Disciplinary staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_discipline`\n\n1. Once the disciplinary handling is complete, close the case: `decided` or\n   `appealed` → `closed`.\n2. `closed_on` is recorded automatically.\n3. Any linked incidents that are not already closed are moved to `closed`.\n4. The case remains as the permanent disciplinary record for the subject.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nIncident: new → attached → closed\n\nCase: draft → under_review → decided → appealed → closed\n              ↘ draft\n\nSuspension: draft → active → expired\n                        ↘ cancelled\n\nSanction: (no state machine — created as final)\n\nFinance Event: draft → confirmed → settled\n                                 → cancelled\n```\n\n## Integration Points\n\n| Integration | Detail |\n|-------------|--------|\n| Match form | Incidents tab is available on matches |\n| Player form | Discipline tab shows player history |\n| Match sheets | Active suspensions block player eligibility |\n| Standings | Point-deduction sanctions feed standing adjustments |\n| Finance | Fine sanctions create or update finance events |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md) — incident capture and match-sheet eligibility effects\n- [Governance Override](WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md) — appeal or exception handling\n- [Financial Tracking](WORKFLOW_FINANCIAL_TRACKING.md) — fine payment tracking\n", "content_length": 6045, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_DISCIPLINE_PIPELINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "b07ab13c6f621478e86cc1b1b41fdeb9143345198324a9e7f07608ace0df4540", "size_bytes": 6093}
- {"content": "# Workflow: Financial Tracking\n\nLightweight financial event recording for registration fees, disciplinary fines,\nreferee reimbursements, and other federation-related financial activity.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe federation needs to track money flowing in and out — registration fees from\nclubs, fines from disciplinary actions, reimbursements for referees — without\nrequiring a full accounting module. The finance bridge module records these as\n**finance events** linked to their source, with states that prepare them for\nfuture accounting integration.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Fee types, finance events |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs (fee payers) |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players (registration fees) |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament context |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referees (reimbursements) |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Sanctions (fines) |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Finance confirmation notifications |\n| `sports_federation_reporting` | Financial summary reports |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Fee Type Catalogue Setup\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_finance_bridge`\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Finance → Fee Types**.\n2. Create fee type entries:\n\n| Example | Category | Default Amount |\n|---------|----------|---------------|\n| Season Registration Fee | `registration` | €250.00 |\n| Player License Fee | `registration` | €25.00 |\n| Disciplinary Fine (Yellow Card) | `fine` | €50.00 |\n| Disciplinary Fine (Red Card) | `fine` | €150.00 |\n| Referee Travel Reimbursement | `reimbursement` | €75.00 |\n| Match Officials Fee | `reimbursement` | €100.00 |\n| Venue Booking (passthrough) | `other` | variable |\n\nEach fee type has a unique code, category, and default amount.\n\n### 2. Verify amounts, source references, and the deterministic `external_ref`.\n3. **Confirm**: state `draft` → `confirmed`.\n4. Confirmed events represent accepted financial obligations.\n5. When an exception is\nlegitimate, the governance module captures it as a formal **override request**\nso the justification, decision, implementation, and outcome stay visible after\nthe immediate issue is resolved.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests, decisions, audit notes, outcomes |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core records referenced by requests |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament and match references |\n| `mail` | Chatter tracking on requests |\n\n## Common Override Scenarios\n\n| Scenario | Example |\n|----------|---------|\n| Late registration | Club missed the deadline but has a valid reason |\n| Eligibility waiver | Player needs an exception to a standard rule |\n| Result correction | Approved result requires governance-backed correction |\n| Standing adjustment | Federation needs a formal ranking correction |\n| Administrative forfeit | A match outcome must be imposed administratively |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Override Request Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation official or authorised user\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Governance → Override Requests**.\n2. Create a new request with:\n   - title\n   - request type\n   - target record (`target_model` / `target_res_id`)\n   - justification in `reason`\n3. The requester and request timestamp are recorded automatically.\n4. The request starts in `draft`.\n\n### 2. Submission And Withdrawal\n\n**Actor**: Requester\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. Review the draft for completeness.\n2. Submit the request: `draft` → `submitted`.\n3. If the request needs correction before a decision is made, use **Withdraw**\n   to return it from `submitted` to `draft`.\n\nThe withdraw path is only available while the request is still `submitted`.\n\n### 3. Governance Decision\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. Review the submitted request, target record, and supporting context.\n2. Add audit notes if the review needs extra findings or commentary.\n3. Decide the request while it is still `submitted`:\n   - **Approve**: `submitted` → `approved`\n   - **Reject**: `submitted` → `rejected`\n4. The standard approve/reject actions create a decision record automatically.\n\nThere is no separate `under_review` state in the current model. Operationally,\nreview happens while the request remains `submitted`.\n\n### 4. Implementation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance` plus the affected owning module\n\n1. If approved, implement the exception in the relevant workflow.\n2. Record the operational note in `implementation_note` when useful.\n3. Mark the request implemented: `approved` → `implemented`.\n4. Implementation writes an outcome-log row so later review can see what was\n   actually done, not just what was approved.\n\n### 5. Closure\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer or federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. Once follow-up is complete, close the request.\n2. Only `implemented` or `rejected` requests can move to `closed`.\n\n## Audit Trail\n\nThe complete audit trail includes:\n\n- request creation with requester and timestamp\n- submission and any withdrawal back to draft\n- approval or rejection decision rows\n- audit notes with author and timestamp\n- implementation notes and outcome-log rows\n- chatter log of tracked state changes\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nOverride Request: draft → submitted → approved → implemented → closed\n                         ↘ draft     ↘ rejected → closed\n\nDecision: approved / rejected\n          (recorded when the request leaves submitted)\n```\n\n## Security Model\n\n| Group | Permissions |\n|-------|-------------|\n| Federation Staff | Can create override requests |\n| Governance Officer | Can review, approve, reject, and close requests |\n\n## Generic Target\n\nOverride requests use a **model/res_id pattern** and can link to many record\ntypes, including:\n\n- `federation.season.registration` — late registration exception\n- `federation.player` — eligibility waiver\n- `federation.match` — result correction or replay follow-up\n- `federation.sanction` — discipline exception handling\n- `federation.team.roster` — roster limit exception\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Result Pipeline](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — contested results may require governance action\n- [Discipline Pipeline](WORKFLOW_DISCIPLINE_PIPELINE.md) — disciplinary appeals or exception handling\n- [Season Registration](WORKFLOW_SEASON_REGISTRATION.md) — late registration exceptions\n- [Compliance Management](WORKFLOW_COMPLIANCE_MANAGEMENT.md) — compliance exceptions\n\n## Unified Recovery Model\n\nWhen operational data has already been published, handle exceptions in one\nconsistent operator model:\n\n1. Raise dispute/request exception from the owning record.\n2. Approve or reject through Governance Override.\n3. If approved, implement the owning-record correction.\n4. Re-run result and standings pipeline as needed.\n5. Recover publication state by republishing the affected standings/tournament\n   surfaces.\n", "content_length": 5608, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "fd351ce6d78617aa495dcb3799c140394c890b3a3714a1a19df7bb075fb08074", "size_bytes": 5652}

This workflow covers\nthe operational sequence from pre-match preparation through to the final whistle.\n\nPrimary surfaces by phase:\n\n- **Preparation** — start from the portal **Club Operations Workspace** or team\n   workspace for squad sheets and roster readiness. The **Preparation Queue** is\n   a direct shortcut when the operator already knows they only need pre-kick-off\n   tasks, and the backend **Gameday Planner** is the staff-only day-level\n   surface for slot assignment and final one-day adjustments.\n- **Live operations** — use the **Live Operations Board** at\n   `/sports/competitions/<edition-slug>/operations` once matches are underway.\n- **Result follow-up** — use the portal **Result Follow-Up Queue** after full\n   time when results still need approval, contests, or standings follow-up.\n   Backend match and tournament records are specialist follow-up surfaces, not\n   the default club starting point.\n\nDirect queues and record pages exist as shortcuts, but they should not be\ntreated as equal-weight starting points for club representatives.\n\nDraft match days may be deleted during preparation. Any draft or\nchange-requested working schedules are removed with the match day so the\nrestrictive schedule foreign key cannot leave an unusable planning record.\nMatch days with review or publication history, or with live operations, remain\nprotected and must use schedule revision or operational correction workflows.\n\nFor test cleanup or an explicitly authorized destructive correction, a closed\nmatch day exposes **Delete Match Day** to federation and match-day managers. The\nwizard reports the affected schedule, publication, session, deviation, and\nmatch counts before requiring a reason and showing a final confirmation popup.\nIt removes the match-day execution and publication evidence, while retaining\ncompetition match records detached from the deleted publication and slots.\n\n## Operational Control Layer\n\nThe portal action-items page (`/my/action-items`) is a compact control layer\nover the preparation and result follow-up phases. It projects unresolved work\nfrom the authoritative registration, roster, club-duty, and result records\ninto `federation.operation.task` records. Re-running synchronization is\nidempotent; resolving a source closes its task, while a newly blocking source\nstate reopens the same task by its stable source key.\n\nClub representatives receive only tasks for clubs they represent. Federation\nmanagers use the backend Operational Action Queue to filter blocking work by\nclub, tournament, type, priority, deadline, and state. A task acknowledgement\ndoes not override a sporting blocker; the linked domain action remains the\nrequired resolution path.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_rosters` | Season rosters and match-day squad sheets |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referee assignment to matches |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue and playing-area assignment |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Match record management |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player eligibility verification |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Squad-size limits and eligibility rules |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Suspension checks |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Referee assignment emails and staffing alert activities |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Roster Preparation (Pre-Season)\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. Create a **team roster** for the season/competition.\n2. Link to the team, season, and optionally the competition and rule set.\n3. Add **roster lines** — each line links a player and can mark captain or vice-captain responsibilities.\n4. Validate squad size and player eligibility against the rule set, including\n   season registration, suspensions, and season/club-scoped license checks.\n5. Portal roster editing only offers licenses that match the selected roster,\n   season, and player, and manually posted hidden ids are rejected by the same\n   server-side scope.\n6. Review readiness feedback and set roster status: `draft` → `active`.\n7. An active roster is the pool from which match sheets draw players.\n\n### 2. Match Sheet Creation\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or team manager\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. For each match, create a **match sheet** for each participating team (home/away).\n2. Link the match sheet to the match, team, and source roster.\n3. Set the side (`home` or `away`).\n4. Add **match sheet lines** — typically by selecting active roster lines from\n   the team's source roster.\n5. Mark starters vs. substitutes.\n6. Assign jersey numbers and captaincy where needed.\n7. Add coach and manager names.\n8. Validate: selected players must belong to active roster lines for the same\n   team, satisfy license and registration rules for the match context, and any\n   blockers are shown as readable feedback before submission.\n9. If a submitted sheet needs correction, use **Reset to Draft**, update the\n   lineup, and resubmit. Only `submitted` sheets can take this correction path.\n10. After approval, the sheet lineup is frozen; only substitution timing fields\n    remain editable until the sheet is explicitly locked.\n\nMatch sheet states: `draft` → `submitted` → `approved` → `locked`.\n\nPortal workspace note:\n\n- Club representatives using the tournament workspace only see match-day tasks\n   for active tournaments (`open` or `in_progress`) and for teams inside their\n   current whole-club scope or explicit current team scope. Inactive or expired\n   representative rows do not keep match-day visibility alive.\n\n### 3. Referee Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation referee coordinator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. Select referees from the registry based on certification level and availability.\n2. Create **match referee** assignments with defined roles:\n   - `head` — Main referee\n   - `assistant_1` / `assistant_2` — Assistant referees\n   - `fourth` — Fourth official\n   - `table` — Table or desk official\n3. Each assignment has a state: `draft` (displayed as Assigned) → `confirmed` → `done` / `cancelled`.\n4. Assignments inherit a 48-hour confirmation deadline from the scheduled match time and stay visible as overdue until confirmed, cancelled, or the match closes.\n5. Confirmation is blocked if the official is inactive, their certification is missing / expired for the match date, or another assignment overlaps the same match window.\n6. Matches aggregate readiness from the rule set's `referee_required_count`, confirmed assignments, overdue confirmations, and assignment-level readiness issues.\n7. Scheduling and schedule approval apply these readiness rules before publication: double-booked officials block assignment moves while uncovered availability remains a warning.\n8. Creating an assignment sends an email to the assigned referee with the role and confirmation deadline.\n9. The scheduled notification scan creates federation-manager activities for overdue confirmations and staffing shortages.\n10. SQL constraint prevents duplicate (match, referee, role) combinations.\n11. The rule set's `referee_required_count` indicates how many officials are needed.\n\nFor automatic club-duty allocation, a club is considered to be playing during\nthe target match whenever one of its teams is assigned to a published match\nwhose time window overlaps the target window, even when the matches use\ndifferent courts. The allocator therefore prefers an eligible club outside\nthe whole concurrent set, not merely outside the target match's two clubs.\n\n### 4. Venue Confirmation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_venues`\n\n1. Confirm the match venue is set (via `venue_id` on the match).\n2. Verify the playing area is available and suitable.\n   - Calendar capacity preparation excludes unavailable venue or\n      playing-area windows.\n    - Scheduling validates the selected court against the effective division\n       requirements before assignment.\n3. Contact venue via stored contact details if needed.\n4. If the venue incurs passthrough costs, scheduling the match with a venue\n   automatically creates or reuses a draft venue booking finance event. Staff can\n   still call `match.action_create_venue_finance_event()` to adjust the default\n   `venue_booking` charge when needed.\n5. Round scheduling and constraints:\n    - Matches belong to a `federation.tournament.round` (`match.round_id`). The\n       round carries the shared calendar date and venue; each match keeps the\n       exact kickoff time and optional playing area.\n    - The venues module enforces a constraint that prevents teams in the same\n       `category` from playing the same opponent more than once inside the same\n       round. This avoids repeated pairings in one shared round block.\n    - Updating a round's venue propagates that venue to its matches. Updating a\n       round's date preserves each match's time-of-day while moving the match to\n       the round's calendar date.\n\n### 5. Pre-Match Checks\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff\n**Modules**: Multiple\n\nBefore the match starts, verify:\n\n| Check | Module | Detail |\n|-------|--------|--------|\n| Match sheets submitted | `rosters` | Both teams have approved sheets |\n| Squad sizes valid | `rules` | Within min/max from rule set |\n| Player licenses active | `people` | All listed players have active season licenses |\n| No active suspensions | `discipline` | No player on the sheet is currently suspended |\n| Referees confirmed | `officiating` | Required referee roles are filled, confirmable, and not double-booked |\n| Venue set | `venues` | Match has a valid venue assignment that avoids blackout and capability issues |\n\nOperational traceability additions:\n\n- Once a roster line is used on a submitted, approved, or locked match sheet,\n   that referenced roster line can no longer be structurally changed or removed.\n- Match sheets record substitution timing (`entered_minute`, `left_minute`) on\n   the declared squad instead of adding late lineup changes.\n- Roster and match-sheet lifecycle events are written to participation audit\n   history so club reps and staff can review what changed and when.\n\n### 6. Match Execution\n\n**Actor**: Referees, federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Set match state to `in_progress` at kick-off.\n2. During the match, record:\n   - Substitutions (update `entered_minute` / `left_minute` on approved match-sheet lines)\n   - Incidents (yellow/red cards, misconduct) → feeds into discipline workflow\n3. At full time, enter final scores (`home_score`, `away_score`).\n4. Set match state to `done`.\n\n### 7. Post-Match Actions\n\n**Actor**: Various\n**Modules**: Multiple\n\nAfter the match completes:\n\n| Action | Module | Detail |\n|--------|--------|--------|\n| Lock match sheets | `rosters` | Sheets move to `locked` state |\n| Complete referee assignments | `officiating` | Assignments marked `done` |\n| Submit result for verification | `result_control` | Feeds into result pipeline |\n| Record incidents | `discipline` | Incidents logged during match |\n| Log finance events | `finance_bridge` | Reimbursements for assignments marked `done`, venue booking charges for scheduled venue matches, and any linked fines |\n| Recompute standings | `standings` | Updated with new result |\n\nOperational readiness additions:\n\n- Match forms expose official counts, overdue confirmations, and aggregated readiness issues so staffing gaps remain visible before kick-off.\n- The notification scan creates follow-up activities for overdue confirmations and matches that still fail the officiating readiness check.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nRoster: draft ↔ active → closed → active\n\nMatch Sheet: draft → submitted → approved → locked\n                          ↘ draft\n\nReferee Assignment:
