This workflow covers\nthe operational sequence from pre-match preparation through to the final whistle.\n\nPrimary surfaces by phase:\n\n- **Preparation** — start from the portal **Club Operations Workspace** or team\n   workspace for squad sheets and roster readiness. The **Preparation Queue** is\n   a direct shortcut when the operator already knows they only need pre-kick-off\n   tasks, and the backend **Gameday Planner** is the staff-only day-level\n   surface for slot assignment and final one-day adjustments.\n- **Live operations** — use the **Live Operations Board** at\n   `/sports/competitions/<edition-slug>/operations` once matches are underway.\n- **Result follow-up** — use the portal **Result Follow-Up Queue** after full\n   time when results still need approval, contests, or standings follow-up.\n   Backend match and tournament records are specialist follow-up surfaces, not\n   the default club starting point.\n\nDirect queues and record pages exist as shortcuts, but they should not be\ntreated as equal-weight starting points for club representatives.\n\nDraft match days may be deleted during preparation. Any draft or\nchange-requested working schedules are removed with the match day so the\nrestrictive schedule foreign key cannot leave an unusable planning record.\nMatch days with review or publication history, or with live operations, remain\nprotected and must use schedule revision or operational correction workflows.\n\nFor test cleanup or an explicitly authorized destructive correction, a closed\nmatch day exposes **Delete Match Day** to federation and match-day managers. The\nwizard reports the affected schedule, publication, session, deviation, and\nmatch counts before requiring a reason and showing a final confirmation popup.\nIt removes the match-day execution and publication evidence, while retaining\ncompetition match records detached from the deleted publication and slots.\n\n## Operational Control Layer\n\nThe portal action-items page (`/my/action-items`) is a compact control layer\nover the preparation and result follow-up phases. It projects unresolved work\nfrom the authoritative registration, roster, club-duty, and result records\ninto `federation.operation.task` records. Re-running synchronization is\nidempotent; resolving a source closes its task, while a newly blocking source\nstate reopens the same task by its stable source key.\n\nClub representatives receive only tasks for clubs they represent. Federation\nmanagers use the backend Operational Action Queue to filter blocking work by\nclub, tournament, type, priority, deadline, and state. A task acknowledgement\ndoes not override a sporting blocker; the linked domain action remains the\nrequired resolution path.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_rosters` | Season rosters and match-day squad sheets |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referee assignment to matches |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue and playing-area assignment |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Match record management |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player eligibility verification |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Squad-size limits and eligibility rules |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Suspension checks |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Referee assignment emails and staffing alert activities |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Roster Preparation (Pre-Season)\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. Create a **team roster** for the season/competition.\n2. Link to the team, season, and optionally the competition and rule set.\n3. Add **roster lines** — each line links a player and can mark captain or vice-captain responsibilities.\n4. Validate squad size and player eligibility against the rule set, including\n   season registration, suspensions, and season/club-scoped license checks.\n5. Portal roster editing only offers licenses that match the selected roster,\n   season, and player, and manually posted hidden ids are rejected by the same\n   server-side scope.\n6. Review readiness feedback and set roster status: `draft` → `active`.\n7. An active roster is the pool from which match sheets draw players.\n\n### 2. Match Sheet Creation\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or team manager\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. For each match, create a **match sheet** for each participating team (home/away).\n2. Link the match sheet to the match, team, and source roster.\n3. Set the side (`home` or `away`).\n4. Add **match sheet lines** — typically by selecting active roster lines from\n   the team's source roster.\n5. Mark starters vs. substitutes.\n6. Assign jersey numbers and captaincy where needed.\n7. Add coach and manager names.\n8. Validate: selected players must belong to active roster lines for the same\n   team, satisfy license and registration rules for the match context, and any\n   blockers are shown as readable feedback before submission.\n9. If a submitted sheet needs correction, use **Reset to Draft**, update the\n   lineup, and resubmit. Only `submitted` sheets can take this correction path.\n10. After approval, the sheet lineup is frozen; only substitution timing fields\n    remain editable until the sheet is explicitly locked.\n\nMatch sheet states: `draft` → `submitted` → `approved` → `locked`.\n\nPortal workspace note:\n\n- Club representatives using the tournament workspace only see match-day tasks\n   for active tournaments (`open` or `in_progress`) and for teams inside their\n   current whole-club scope or explicit current team scope. Inactive or expired\n   representative rows do not keep match-day visibility alive.\n\n### 3. Referee Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation referee coordinator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. Select referees from the registry based on certification level and availability.\n2. Create **match referee** assignments with defined roles:\n   - `head` — Main referee\n   - `assistant_1` / `assistant_2` — Assistant referees\n   - `fourth` — Fourth official\n   - `table` — Table or desk official\n3. Each assignment has a state: `draft` (displayed as Assigned) → `confirmed` → `done` / `cancelled`.\n4. Assignments inherit a 48-hour confirmation deadline from the scheduled match time and stay visible as overdue until confirmed, cancelled, or the match closes.\n5. Confirmation is blocked if the official is inactive, their certification is missing / expired for the match date, or another assignment overlaps the same match window.\n6. Matches aggregate readiness from the rule set's `referee_required_count`, confirmed assignments, overdue confirmations, and assignment-level readiness issues.\n7. Scheduling and schedule approval apply these readiness rules before publication: double-booked officials block assignment moves while uncovered availability remains a warning.\n8. Creating an assignment sends an email to the assigned referee with the role and confirmation deadline.\n9. The scheduled notification scan creates federation-manager activities for overdue confirmations and staffing shortages.\n10. SQL constraint prevents duplicate (match, referee, role) combinations.\n11. The rule set's `referee_required_count` indicates how many officials are needed.\n\nFor automatic club-duty allocation, a club is considered to be playing during\nthe target match whenever one of its teams is assigned to a published match\nwhose time window overlaps the target window, even when the matches use\ndifferent courts. The allocator therefore prefers an eligible club outside\nthe whole concurrent set, not merely outside the target match's two clubs.\n\n### 4. Venue Confirmation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_venues`\n\n1. Confirm the match venue is set (via `venue_id` on the match).\n2. Verify the playing area is available and suitable.\n   - Calendar capacity preparation excludes unavailable venue or\n      playing-area windows.\n    - Scheduling validates the selected court against the effective division\n       requirements before assignment.\n3. Contact venue via stored contact details if needed.\n4. If the venue incurs passthrough costs, scheduling the match with a venue\n   automatically creates or reuses a draft venue booking finance event. Staff can\n   still call `match.action_create_venue_finance_event()` to adjust the default\n   `venue_booking` charge when needed.\n5. Round scheduling and constraints:\n    - Matches belong to a `federation.tournament.round` (`match.round_id`). The\n       round carries the shared calendar date and venue; each match keeps the\n       exact kickoff time and optional playing area.\n    - The venues module enforces a constraint that prevents teams in the same\n       `category` from playing the same opponent more than once inside the same\n       round. This avoids repeated pairings in one shared round block.\n    - Updating a round's venue propagates that venue to its matches. Updating a\n       round's date preserves each match's time-of-day while moving the match to\n       the round's calendar date.\n\n### 5. Pre-Match Checks\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff\n**Modules**: Multiple\n\nBefore the match starts, verify:\n\n| Check | Module | Detail |\n|-------|--------|--------|\n| Match sheets submitted | `rosters` | Both teams have approved sheets |\n| Squad sizes valid | `rules` | Within min/max from rule set |\n| Player licenses active | `people` | All listed players have active season licenses |\n| No active suspensions | `discipline` | No player on the sheet is currently suspended |\n| Referees confirmed | `officiating` | Required referee roles are filled, confirmable, and not double-booked |\n| Venue set | `venues` | Match has a valid venue assignment that avoids blackout and capability issues |\n\nOperational traceability additions:\n\n- Once a roster line is used on a submitted, approved, or locked match sheet,\n   that referenced roster line can no longer be structurally changed or removed.\n- Match sheets record substitution timing (`entered_minute`, `left_minute`) on\n   the declared squad instead of adding late lineup changes.\n- Roster and match-sheet lifecycle events are written to participation audit\n   history so club reps and staff can review what changed and when.\n\n### 6. Match Execution\n\n**Actor**: Referees, federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Set match state to `in_progress` at kick-off.\n2. During the match, record:\n   - Substitutions (update `entered_minute` / `left_minute` on approved match-sheet lines)\n   - Incidents (yellow/red cards, misconduct) → feeds into discipline workflow\n3. At full time, enter final scores (`home_score`, `away_score`).\n4. Set match state to `done`.\n\n### 7. Post-Match Actions\n\n**Actor**: Various\n**Modules**: Multiple\n\nAfter the match completes:\n\n| Action | Module | Detail |\n|--------|--------|--------|\n| Lock match sheets | `rosters` | Sheets move to `locked` state |\n| Complete referee assignments | `officiating` | Assignments marked `done` |\n| Submit result for verification | `result_control` | Feeds into result pipeline |\n| Record incidents | `discipline` | Incidents logged during match |\n| Log finance events | `finance_bridge` | Reimbursements for assignments marked `done`, venue booking charges for scheduled venue matches, and any linked fines |\n| Recompute standings | `standings` | Updated with new result |\n\nOperational readiness additions:\n\n- Match forms expose official counts, overdue confirmations, and aggregated readiness issues so staffing gaps remain visible before kick-off.\n- The notification scan creates follow-up activities for overdue confirmations and matches that still fail the officiating readiness check.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nRoster: draft ↔ active → closed → active\n\nMatch Sheet: draft → submitted → approved → locked\n                          ↘ draft\n\nReferee Assignment: assigned → confirmed → done\n                                          → cancelled\n\nMatch: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done\n                                    → cancelled\n```\n\n## Typical internal federation staff via their normal Odoo session.\n- **Entry points**: open from the backend tournament form or from the club/team\n   workspace once preparation is complete. each card shows teams, score, state, referee, and one primary action |\n| Result entry panel | Sticky side panel on desktop and bottom-sheet task panel on compact screens for fast score entry and result actions |\n| Filters | Search by team name; filter by court, match state, result state, timeline, referee |\n\nAdditional operator guidance:\n\n- each match card surfaces a server-computed **Next step** so volunteers do not need to infer the immediate action from raw state badges alone.\n- compact screens keep the board overview first; the task panel opens only after the operator selects a match.\n- keyboard shortcuts are available for rapid desk work: `Alt + ↑ / Alt + ↓` moves between ranked tasks and `Ctrl/Cmd + S` runs the selected panel's main action.\n\n### How results are saved\n\nResult saves on the operations board call the existing result-control action methods on the server:\n\n- `action_submit_result` — submits a score for verification\n- `action_verify_result` — marks result verified by a validator\n- `action_approve_result` — approves and counts in standings\n- `action_contest_result` — contests an approved result\n- `action_correct_result` — corrects a contested result\n\nAll validation and workflow state guards remain server-side. Standings recomputation is triggered by the existing hooks in `sports_federation_result_control` on approve/contest/correct.\n\n### Known limitations and follow-up ideas\n\n- Live push (Odoo bus) is not implemented; the board polls every 60 s.\n- Referee assignment workflow is not exposed on the board; use the existing officiating views.\n- Bracket visualization and drag-and-drop court scheduling are not in scope for this version.\n- QR-code per court, offline-first result capture, and pool standings preview are follow-up ideas.\n\n\n## Schedule approval handoff\n\nBefore match-day preparation can start, the planner submits the complete working\nschedule through **Submit for Review**. Approval revalidation reads\nthe submitted schedule's calendar and venue data internally; venue or calendar\nmanagement rights are not required. - {"content": "# Workflow: Officiating\n\nEnd-to-end lifecycle for managing referees — from certification registration\nthrough match assignment, confirmation, completion, and shortage alerting.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe **officiating** domain tracks referees (`federation.referee`), their\ncertification records (`federation.referee.certification`), and per-match role\nassignments (`federation.match.referee`). When a referee is assigned to a\nmatch, they receive an automated notification. If the assignment is not\nconfirmed before the deadline, the system flags it as overdue and optionally\nsends an alert to the referee coordinator.\n\nThis is a specialist coordinator workflow, not the primary day-to-day starting\nsurface for club representatives. Club operators should usually encounter\nofficiating readiness through the phase-specific workspaces and alerts rather\nthan begin from officiating lists.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referee registry, certifications, match assignments |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Match records |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Referee assignment and shortage alert dispatching |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `federation.referee` | Master referee record with contact info and certification level |\n| `federation.referee.certification` | Dated certification for a specific officiating level |\n| `federation.match.referee` | Assignment of one referee to one match in a specific role |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Referee Registration\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Officiating → Referees** and click **New**.\n2. Enter name, contact details (email, phone, mobile).\n3. Set `certification_level` to the highest level held:\n   `local` | `regional` | `national` | `international`.\n4. Save. The referee is immediately available for match assignments.\n\n### 2. Certification Records\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. On the referee form, open the **Certifications** tab.\n2. Add one `federation.referee.certification` line per certification granted:\n   - Certification number (unique per referee / level / issue date)\n   - Level (matches the levels on the referee itself)\n   - Issue date and optional expiry date\n   - Issuing body\n3. Active certifications (`active = True`) are considered valid.\n4. An expired certification (`expiry_date` in the past) should be archived\n   (`active = False`) by an admin; the system does not auto-archive.\n\nCertification uniqueness: `(referee_id, level, issue_date)` — one certification\nper level per issuance date.\n\n### 3. Match Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation referee coordinator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. Open the match record in **Federation → Tournaments → Matches**.\n2. In the **Referees** tab (or from the Referees list), click **Add a line**.\n3. Select the referee and assign a **role**:\n   - `head` — Head Referee\n   - `assistant_1` / `assistant_2` — Assistant Referees\n   - `fourth` — Fourth Official\n   - `table` — Table Official\n4. Save. The assignment starts in state **`draft`** (\"Assigned\").\n5. On creation, the notification dispatcher fires `send_referee_assigned` if\n   `federation.notification.dispatcher` is available, sending an assignment\n   notice to the referee.\n\nAssignment uniqueness: `(match_id, referee_id, role)` — one role per referee per match.\n\n### 4. Readiness Check\n\n**Actor**: System (computed field)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\nAfter assignment, the system computes:\n- `confirmation_deadline` — 48 hours before the scheduled match kickoff.\n- `is_confirmation_overdue` — True if past deadline and still in `draft`.\n- `assignment_ready` — True when the assignment is `confirmed`, the referee\n  is active, and holds a valid certification for the match's required level.\n- `readiness_feedback` — human-readable summary of any blocking reasons.\n\nThese fields re-compute whenever match scheduling, referee certification, or\nassignment state changes.\n\n### 5. Referee Confirmation\n\n**Actor**: Referee or federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. Referee or administrator sets the assignment state: **`draft` → `confirmed`**.\n2. `confirmed_on` timestamp is recorded.\n3. `assignment_ready` becomes True (assuming valid certification and active referee).\n\n### 6. Overdue / Shortage Detection\n\n**Actor**: System (notification scan) or administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating` + `sports_federation_notifications`\n\n1. Assignments with `is_confirmation_overdue = True` are surfaced as a warning\n   in the coordinator's dashboard and in the readiness feedback.\n2. If the `sports_federation_notifications` module is installed, a scheduled\n   notification scan can detect unconfirmed assignments and send alerts.\n3. The coordinator resolves shortages by:\n   - Following up with the originally assigned referee, OR\n   - Cancelling the assignment (`draft` → `cancelled`) and assigning a replacement.\n\n### 7. Match Completion\n\n**Actor**: System or federation administrator (after match result entry)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. When a match is completed (state → `done`), assignments are marked **`done`**.\n2. `completed_on` timestamp is recorded.\n3. `done` assignments contribute to `assignment_count` on the referee record for\n   performance and reporting purposes.\n\n### 8. Cancellation\n\n**Actor**: Federation coordinator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\n1. Any assignment in `draft` or `confirmed` can be cancelled by setting state → **`cancelled`**.\n2. `cancelled_on` timestamp is recorded.\n3. Cancelled assignments remain in the record for audit purposes but are excluded\n   from the assignment count and readiness checks.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nAssignment: draft (Assigned) → confirmed → done\n                             ↘ cancelled\n            draft → cancelled\n```\n\n## Certification States\n\n```\nCertification: active=True  (valid, current)\n               active=False (archived/expired — set manually by administrator)\n```\n\n## Notification Triggers\n\n| Event | Notification |\n|-------|-------------|\n| Assignment created | `send_referee_assigned` via notification dispatcher |\n| Assignment overdue | Alert to referee coordinator (notification scan) |\n\n## Key Decision Points\n\n| Question | Outcome |\n|----------|---------|\n| No active certification at required level? | `assignment_ready = False`; readiness feedback lists reason |\n| Confirmation deadline passed, still `draft`? | `is_confirmation_overdue = True`; flagged in dashboard |\n| Another assignment overlaps the same match window? | `assignment_ready = False`; confirmation is blocked until the clash is resolved |\n| Match cancelled? | Coordinator cancels all assignments; `cancelled_on` recorded |\n| Referee deactivated (`active = False`)? | All future assignments blocked; `assignment_ready = False` |\n\n## Referee Availability & Self-Service (Specialist / Planned)\n\n> **Note**: The availability model is a planned feature. The fields and steps\n> below describe the intended design; the `federation.referee.availability`\n> model may not yet be present in all installations. Check the module README\n> for the current implementation status.\n\n### Marking Availability Windows\n\n**Actor**: Referee (portal) or federation coordinator (back office)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating` + `sports_federation_portal`\n\n1. Referee logs into the federation portal.\n2. Navigates to **My Availability** in the officiating section.\n3. Creates `federation.referee.availability` records specifying:\n   - **Start** and **End** datetime of the available window\n   - Optional notes (e.g. \"available only from 14:00\")\n4. Saves. Availability records are immediately visible to the coordinator.\n\nAlternatively, the coordinator creates availability records on behalf of the\nreferee from the back office (**Federation → Officiating → Referees → Availability tab**).\n\n### Assignment Engine Conflict Check\n\n**Actor**: System (at assignment creation time)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating`\n\nWhen the coordinator assigns a referee to a match:\n\n1. The system checks whether the match's scheduled kickoff falls within any\n   `federation.referee.availability` window for that referee.\n2. If the match falls **outside** all recorded availability windows, a warning\n   is shown on the assignment form: *\"No availability record covers this match\n   slot.\"*\n3. The coordinator can override the warning and save the assignment (warnings\n   do not block creation).\n4. If no availability records exist for a referee, no conflict check is\n   performed and no warning is raised.\n5. If the referee is already assigned to another match that overlaps the same\n   assignment window, the draft assignment can still be recorded for follow-up,\n   but `assignment_ready` becomes `False` and confirmation is blocked until the\n   clash is resolved.\n6. The scheduling workflow reuses the same officiating checks so double-booking\n   blocks schedule readiness while uncovered availability remains visible as a\n   warning. The officiating addon remains the owner of these checks.\n\n### Portal Accept / Decline Flow\n\n**Actor**: Referee (portal)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating` + `sports_federation_portal`\n\nAfter an assignment is created in `draft` state and the referee receives the\nassignment notification:\n\n1. Referee opens the notification or navigates to **My Assignments** in the portal.\n   - The portal assignments list highlights one explicit **Next step** action\n     (nearest pending response) and shows pending/overdue counters so officials\n     can prioritize urgent confirmations first.\n2. Views the match date, venue, and role.\n3. Clicks **Confirm** or **Decline**:\n   - **Confirm**: assignment state `draft → confirmed`.\n   - **Decline**: assignment state `draft → cancelled`. The coordinator is\n     notified to assign a replacement.\n\nBoth actions are available until the `confirmation_deadline` (48 hours before\nkickoff) passes.\n\n### Confirmation Deadline and Overdue Escalation\n\n**Actor**: System + federation coordinator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_officiating` + `sports_federation_notifications`\n\nIf the referee does not confirm or decline before the `confirmation_deadline`:\n\n1. `is_confirmation_overdue` becomes `True` on the assignment.\n2. The assignment is surfaced in the coordinator's overdue-assignment dashboard\n   filter (**Federation → Officiating → Assignments → Overdue**).\n3. If `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, the scheduled notification\n   scan sends an overdue alert to the coordinator.\n4. The coordinator:\n   - Contacts the referee directly, OR\n   - Cancels the assignment and assigns a replacement.\n\nThere is no auto-cancel on deadline expiry. - {"content": "# Workflow: Player License Lifecycle\n\nEnd-to-end management of a player's federation license — from creation through\nseasonal activation, expiry, suspension checks, and reinstatement.\n\n## Overview\n\nEvery player who competes in a federation tournament must hold a valid\n**player license** (`federation.player.license`) scoped to the current season.\nA license certifies the player's eligibility, links them to their club, and\nrecords their category (Senior, Youth, Junior, Cadet). The license state machine\ndrives eligibility checks used by the roster and rules engines.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player records and license model |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Season and club master data |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Eligibility service (`federation.eligibility.service`) |\n| `sports_federation_rosters` | Roster-line license validation (`assignment_ready`) |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Suspension check integration |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Suspension sanctions that block eligibility |\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | License-fee finance events |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Expiry and reinstatement notifications |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.player.license` | `name` (license number), `player_id`, `season_id`, `club_id`, `state`, `category`, `issue_date`, `expiry_date` |\n| `federation.player` | `state` (`active` / `inactive` / `suspended`), `is_eligible` (computed) |\n\n## License States\n\n```\ndraft → active → expired\n      ↘ cancelled\nactive → cancelled\n```\n\n| State | Meaning |\n|-------|---------|\n| `draft` | License created but not yet active — player is not eligible |\n| `active` | License is valid — player is eligible for roster inclusion |\n| `expired` | Expiry date passed and license was not renewed — player is not eligible |\n| `cancelled` | License administratively voided — player is not eligible |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. License Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator or club representative (portal)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_people`\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → People → Player Licenses** and click **New**, or\n   open the player record and click **Create License** from the **Licenses** tab.\n2. Fill in:\n   - **License Number** — unique identifier (e.g. `LIC-2026-00042`)\n   - **Player** — select the player\n   - **Season** — must be an open season\n   - **Club** — the club the player is registered under this season\n   - **Category** — `Senior`, `Youth`, `Junior`, or `Cadet`\n   - **Issue Date** — defaults to today\n   - **Expiry Date** — set to the season end date or a specific date\n3. Save. The license starts in **`draft`** state.\n\n**Uniqueness constraint**: one license per player per season.\nAttempting a second license for the same player/season raises a validation error.\n\n### 2. Season Activation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_people`\n\n1. After verifying any required compliance documents or fee payments, click\n   **Activate** on the license form.\n2. License state transitions: **`draft` → `active`**.\n3. The player's computed `is_eligible` field becomes `True`.\n4. The player is now available for roster assignment under that season.\n\n**Finance event**: if `sports_federation_finance_bridge` is installed, a license\nfee event (`category = registration`) is created automatically on activation.\n\n### 3. Eligibility Check Integration\n\n**Actor**: System (called by roster and rules modules)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rules`\n\nThe `federation.eligibility.service` is the authoritative eligibility oracle:\n\n1. On roster-line creation or tournament participant validation, the service\n   calls `_is_player_eligible(player, season)`.\n2. The service checks:\n   - `federation.player.license` with `state = active` and matching `season_id`.\n   - `federation.player.state` not equal to `suspended`.\n   - No active suspension sanction from `sports_federation_discipline`.\n3. If any check fails, the roster line is marked `assignment_ready = False` with\n   a human-readable `readiness_feedback`.\n\n### 4. Expiry Rules\n\n**Actor**: System\n**Module**: `sports_federation_people`\n\n- An active license whose `expiry_date` has passed is shown with a visual\n  warning on the player and license forms.\n- The system does **not** auto-transition `active → expired`. An administrator\n  must manually click **Mark Expired** or run the `_cron_expire_licenses`\n  scheduled action (if configured).\n- Expired licenses are excluded from eligibility checks.\n\n**Season close**: when a season is closed, it is good practice to run\n`_cron_expire_licenses` immediately to clean up all active licenses tied to that\nseason.\n\n### 5. Suspension Check Integration\n\n**Actor**: System\n**Module**: `sports_federation_discipline`\n\n1. When a disciplinary sanction with `sanction_type = suspension` and\n   `state = active` exists for a player, the eligibility service flags that\n   player as ineligible regardless of license state.\n2. The player's `state` is set to `suspended` by the discipline module's\n   enforcement action.\n3. All roster lines for that player in upcoming matches are flagged\n   `assignment_ready = False`.\n\n### 6. Reinstatement Path\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_people` + `sports_federation_discipline`\n\nA player can be reinstated after a suspension or licence cancellation:\n\n1. **Suspension ended**: the discipline module expires the suspension sanction\n   and calls `action_reactivate` on the player, transitioning\n   `suspended → active`.\n2. **Cancelled licence renewed**: create a new draft licence for the player,\n   activate it. The old cancelled licence remains in history.\n3. **Expired licence renewed for the same season**: cancel the expired licence,\n   create a new draft licence, and activate it. (The unique constraint is per\n   player/season so the old expired record must be cancelled first.)\n4. On reinstatement, the player's `is_eligible` recomputes automatically.\n\n**Notification**: if `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, the\nreinstatement triggers a notification to the club contact on record.\n\n## Eligibility Summary\n\nA player is eligible to compete when **all** of the following are true:\n\n- `federation.player.state = active`\n- At least one `federation.player.license` with `state = active` and\n  `season_id` matching the competition season\n- No active suspension sanction\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nLicense: draft → active → expired (manual or cron)\n               ↘ cancelled\n         active → cancelled\n\nPlayer:  active → suspended → active (reinstatement)\n         active → inactive\n```\n", "content_length": 6675, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_PLAYER_LICENSE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "6cb3d2a62a95831f6a71074cea52a58211ced4121463d102bcc3327e59ba64f8", "size_bytes": 6731}

Direct queues still exist, but the UI frames them as secondary or\n    advanced paths.\n- Match-day portal labels now reinforce one phase at a time: `Preparation Queue`\n    for pre-kick-off work, `Live Operations Board` for in-progress play, and\n    `Result Follow-Up Queue` for post-match review. Match sheets and raw match\n    records remain direct-access specialist surfaces rather than peer home\n    destinations.\n\n## Guided setup and cross-module handoffs (2026-05-25)\n\n- `sports_federation_base` and `sports_federation_tournament` now use inline\n    banner guidance and richer action help on season, competition,\n    competition-edition, and tournament forms so empty states describe the next\n    valid setup action instead of leaving operators on unexplained lists.\n- `sports_federation_rosters` adds direct operator handoffs from confirmed\n    season registrations into scoped team rosters and from tournament\n    participants into the roster used for readiness checks. The participant form\n    now exposes the roster deadline, current readiness feedback, and the\n    preferred readiness roster in the same place where confirmation can block.\n- `sports_federation_result_control` adds a tournament handoff on match forms so\n    verified, approved, contested, and corrected results can direct staff back\n    to the owning tournament when the next task is standings review or public\n    follow-up rather than another score edit.\n- `sports_federation_standings` and `sports_federation_public_site` now make\n    publication prerequisites visible from the forms themselves: standings pages\n    explain whether approved results are still missing or whether publication is\n    the next step, while tournament and standings Website tabs differentiate\n    between unpublished tournaments, unpublished standings, and hidden\n    standings, with direct links back to the relevant standings action.\n\nCanonical readiness and handoff chain:\n\n1. Season registration confirmation\n2. Tournament participant confirmation\n3. Roster and match-day readiness\n4. Result approval\n5. Standings review/recompute\n6. Tournament and standings publication\n\nBlocking vs warning-only standard:\n\n- Blocking: current step cannot proceed until resolved.\n- Warning-only: current step can proceed, but follow-up is required; manager\n    override reason is mandatory where configured (for example publication\n    publication overrides in `sports_federation_schedule_approval`).\n\nException and publication recovery standard:\n\n- Governance Override is the canonical exception engine.\n- After disputed/corrected outcomes, use one recovery loop: resolve exception,\n    restore result/standings officiality, then republish affected public surfaces.\n\n## Canonical planning and match-day flows (2026-05-25)\n\n- `sports_federation_registration` finalizes participant sets for a competition.\n- `sports_federation_format` freezes the versioned logical structure and stage\n    graph.\n- `sports_federation_calendar` prepares physical match days, capacity, and slots.\n- `sports_federation_scheduling` validates and proposes deterministic fixture\n    assignments.\n- `sports_federation_schedule_approval` reviews schedules and publishes an\n    immutable snapshot; `sports_federation_matchday` executes only that snapshot.\n- `sports_federation_portal` now names three distinct club-operator phases:\n    match-day preparation in the workspace or preparation queue, live play in\n    the live operations board, and result follow-up in the results queue. Those\n    portal surfaces now explain when operators should move from one phase to the\n    next instead of presenting the routes as equal-weight peers.\n\n## competition planning flow (2026-05-25)\n\nThe competition workflow is implemented by small, role-owned addons rather\nthan a monolithic workspace service. Each handover is explicit and the server\nremains authoritative for validation and publication.\n\n### Phase completion snapshot\n\n- Registration finalizes a participant set before format work begins.\n- Format creates a versioned structure and stage graph; it does not create\n    physical slots.\n- Calendar creates physical match days and slots from capacity and timeline\n    rules.\n- Scheduling accepts the frozen structure and calendar capacity, then writes\n    validated fixture-to-slot assignments through its server-side commands.\n- Approval is a separate review boundary and stores the immutable publication\n    snapshot. Match-day commands reject unpublished or superseded schedules.\n- Portal and officiating modules extend their own surfaces without becoming the\n    authoritative owner of competition transitions.\n\n### Retired competition-core view cleanup (2026-08-27)\n\nCompetition Core version `19.0.1.3.0` removes the database UI records left\nbehind by the retired competition engine before current division views are\nvalidated. This is required because Odoo does not automatically delete records\nwhose XML IDs disappear from a module's data files. The migration is\nidempotent and preserves the current role-assignment and competition-history\nactions.\n\n## Portal/public intuitiveness baseline (2026-05-26)\n\n- `sports_federation_portal/models/portal_status_labels.py` now centralizes\n    human-facing labels for tournament, registration, participant, match,\n    result-state, sheet, officiating assignment, duty, player, and license\n    states.\n- Portal templates now render state labels via model helper methods instead of\n    direct selection dictionaries or raw `state`/`result_state` values.\n- `sports_federation_public_site/models/public_status_labels.py` now includes\n    public-facing license state labels so club/player public pages avoid raw\n    internal status rendering.\n- Regression guards in portal/public template accessibility tests now block\n    reintroduction of raw internal state render fragments.\n- Intuitiveness governance follows the documentation and terminology review\n    expectations in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nValidation policy\n\n- Slot occupancy conflicts and team overlap conflicts are blocking.\n- A slot occupancy conflict remains blocking for unscheduled matches, but two\n    already scheduled matches on the same planner root can swap slots when both\n    post-swap validations pass.\n- Short-rest checks use `minimum_rest_minutes` on the division and surface as\n    warnings, not blocking errors.\n- Warning-only assignment overrides and republishing a live schedule require a\n    manager reason that is stored on the planner operation or schedule\n    revision.\n- Validation payloads now include grouped conflict sections, resolution hints,\n    and focus metadata so the UI can highlight the affected slots and matches.\n- Published gamedays protect routine schedule edits for planners.\n- Regression coverage now verifies single and double round-robin generation,\n    knockout generation, locked entry requirements, manager-only competition\n    creation, create-competition input validation, slot generation, blocking\n    overlap rules, short-rest warnings, assignment consistency, publish guards,\n    workspace access control, shared-gameday assignment and planner payload\n    rules, revisioned publication, collaboration heartbeat summaries, grouped\n    validation payloads, and a browser smoke path that creates a competition\n    through the Owl client action.\n\n## Import safety hardening (2026-04-10)\n\nYear 1 Priority 1 item 7 hardened the onboarding and rollover import path in\n`sports_federation_import_tools`.\n\n- All import wizards now share `federation.import.wizard.mixin`, which provides\n    UTF-8 BOM handling, comma or semicolon delimiter support, mapping guidance,\n    shared dry-run statistics, and categorized row-level failure reporting.\n- A new `federation.import.seasons.wizard` covers season creation for annual\n    rollover work, including required-code enforcement and `YYYY-MM-DD` date\n    validation.\n- Club, team, player, and tournament-participant imports now prefer code-based\n    matching when codes are available, which aligns the implementation with the\n    documented onboarding workflow.\n- The player import path no longer attempts to create `federation.player`\n    records with a nonexistent writable `name` field. Imports now populate\n    `first_name` and `last_name`, while still accepting legacy full-name CSVs\n    when they contain both parts.\n- Duplicate rows are intentionally reported and skipped rather than overwritten,\n    so administrators can rehearse and rerun seasonal imports safely.\n\n## Operational reporting expansion (2026-04-10)\n\nYear 1 Priority 1 item 6 expanded reporting from raw CSV extraction into\noperator-facing application reports.\n\n- `sports_federation_reporting` now includes `federation.report.operational`\n    for tournament readiness KPIs across participation, standings coverage,\n    match completion, finance follow-up, and participant-club compliance.\n- Operational KPI rows now include an operator-readable readiness note so the\n    list view and scheduled CSV exports expose the current blocker directly,\n    instead of forcing staff to infer it from raw counts alone.\n- A new `federation.report.standing.reconciliation` view exposes mismatches\n    between confirmed participants and standings coverage, with operator-readable\n    reconciliation notes.\n- A new `federation.report.finance.reconciliation` view turns finance events\n    into a follow-up queue keyed by counterparty, references, age, and\n    completion status instead of only grouped fee totals.\n- `federation.report.schedule` plus a daily cron now generate recurring weekly\n    or monthly CSV snapshots from inside Odoo, so administrators can run the\n    reporting cadence without direct database access.\n- The compliance summary report now exposes `non_compliant_count` so rejected\n    or explicitly failed checks are visible alongside missing, pending, and\n    expired totals.\n\n## Scheduled reporting maintainability extraction (2026-04-21)\n\nThe next highest-value reporting cleanup was to separate schedule orchestration\nfrom per-report row assembly.\n\n- `sports_federation_reporting/services/report_schedule_builders.py` now owns\n    the scheduled-report registry: label metadata, report-row builder\n    functions, list-action XML IDs, season scoping, and any action defaults.\n- `federation.report.schedule` now keeps the stable responsibilities only:\n    cadence windows, CSV serialization, generated-file retention, and typed\n    failure capture for cron or manual runs.\n- Adding a new scheduled report type should now be a single-registry change\n    plus focused tests, instead of editing separate builder and action maps in\n    the model.\n\n## Notification activation (2026-04-10)\n\nYear 1 Priority 1 item 5 converted the notification module from mostly logged\nplaceholders into active workflow delivery.\n\n- `sports_federation_notifications` now sends real emails for season\n    registration decisions, tournament publication, participant confirmation,\n    approved and contested results, frozen standings, finance confirmations,\n    and referee assignments.\n- Result submission now creates validator activities instead of a placeholder\n    log entry, and the scheduled notification scan now creates federation\n    manager activities for overdue referee confirmations and officiating\n    shortages.\n- Shared notification helpers now accept multi-recipient email payloads,\n    deduplicate them, and keep failures non-blocking by writing `failed`\n    notification-log rows instead of rolling back the business action.\n- Suspension issuance remains the only modeled scenario still left as a stub.\n\n## Match-day roster traceability (2026-04-10)\n\nYear 1 Priority 1 item 2 closed the operational gap between season rosters,\nmatch sheets, portal visibility, and disputed results.\n\n- `sports_federation_rosters` now logs roster, lineup, and substitution events\n    in `federation.participation.audit`.\n- Season rosters now expose match-day locking state. Once a live match sheet\n    references a roster line, that referenced line cannot be structurally changed\n    or removed.\n- Approved match sheets now freeze lineup edits while still allowing\n    substitution timing (`entered_minute`, `left_minute`) until final lock.\n- `sports_federation_result_control` now logs every result transition in\n    `federation.match.result.audit`, including dispute and correction reasons.\n- `sports_federation_portal` now exposes read-only roster and match-sheet pages\n    so club representatives can review eligibility blocks, substitutions,\n    participation audit history, and result disputes from the portal.\n\n## Eligibility workflow hardening (2026-04-10)\n\nYear 1 Priority 1 item 1 connected the existing eligibility models to live\nworkflow boundaries instead of leaving them as isolated checks.\n\n- `sports_federation_rules` now evaluates license rules with season, club,\n    selected-license, and reference-date context. Registration rules validate the\n    actual `federation.season.registration` team/season model rather than\n    non-existent player-level registration fields.\n- `sports_federation_rosters` now computes `ready_for_activation` and\n    `readiness_feedback` on rosters. Activation blocks until the active lines meet\n    the rule-set size limits and all players pass eligibility checks.\n- `sports_federation_rosters` now computes `ready_for_submission` and\n    `readiness_feedback` on match sheets. Submission blocks when players are not\n    tied to valid active roster lines, do not satisfy license or registration\n    rules, or the submitted squad size is outside the allowed bounds.\n- `sports_federation_rosters` extends `federation.tournament.participant` so\n    participant confirmation warns before the roster deadline, then requires an\n    active ready roster once that deadline is reached for the tournament\n    season, with competition-specific rosters preferred over generic season\n    rosters.\n- Regression coverage was added for season-aware license checks, team-season\n    registration checks, roster activation gating, match-sheet submission gating,\n    and participant confirmation readiness.\n\n## New competition models and behaviours (2026-04-07)\n\nSeveral new models and scheduling behaviours were added to support more realistic tournaments and automated stage progression:\n\n### Structure stage graph compatibility\n\nThe `sports_federation_format` addon owns the versioned structure graph used by Format Studio. Its stage-to-stage edges are represented by `federation.structure.stage.progression`, with `structure_id`, source-stage, and target-stage relations. This model must not reuse the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` name: the engine model is tournament-oriented and has a different inverse relation contract (`tournament_id`). The distinction allows both addons to be installed in the same registry without field-resolution collisions.\n\nStage-graph ACLs are loaded through the addon's conventional `security/ir.model.access.csv` file. Format Studio's inherited view selects the stage tab structurally by its `stage_ids` field rather than by the translated page label.\n\n- `federation.tournament.round` (in `sports_federation_tournament`) — materialises a logical round inside a stage. Rounds own shared schedule metadata such as sequence and calendar date, and matches attach to them for per-round planning and reporting.\n\n- Round venue extensions (in `sports_federation_venues`) — add `venue_id` to `federation.tournament.round` so venue ownership sits on the same round object that already owns the schedule date and sequence.\n\n- Match bracket/linking fields — `federation.match` now includes: `round_id`, `round_number`, `bracket_position`, `bracket_type`, `source_match_1_id`, `source_match_2_id`, `source_type_1/2` and helper `next_match_ids`. These turn matches into first-class bracket nodes so full knockout trees can be created and wired together programmatically.\n\n- Full knockout bracket generation — the knockout service now constructs a full bracket tree (all rounds) rather than only first-round matches. Placeholder matches for later rounds are created and linked to their source matches (by `source_match_*`); when a match is completed the system will auto-populate winners/losers into the next round using the `action_done()` / `_advance_bracket_teams()` logic.\n\n- Round-robin enhancements — the round-robin service now returns explicit per-round pairings, supports `rounds_count` (repeat full cycles), always materialises `federation.tournament.round` records, and can derive round dates from `schedule_by_round`. Existing stage rounds are reused by sequence order, and when a `venue` string matches a `federation.venue` record the scheduler applies it to the round and linked matches. The service also attempts to alternate `male` / `female` fixtures within a round to provide rest.\n\nImplementation notes\n\n- Round constraints: the `sports_federation_venues` module extends `federation.match` so teams in the same `category` cannot play the same opponent more than once inside the same round. This prevents repeated pairings inside a shared round block.\n\n- Alternation policy: when scheduling by round the scheduler partitions same-gender fixtures and interleaves male/female matches where possible. Mixed-gender fixtures are appended after the alternation. This is a best-effort policy (it preserves determinism but will not re-seed teams).\n\n- Auto-advance: `federation.standing.action_freeze()` triggers any `federation.stage.progression` rules with `auto_advance=True` for the stage/group being frozen — this provides an automated pipeline from computed standings into new stage participants (and is safe-guarded by the progression rule's `state`).\n\n- Venue handling: the `venue` free-text field has been removed from `federation.match`. Use `venue_id` (Many2one to `federation.venue`) instead. The round-robin and knockout wizards accept a venue name string and resolve it to a `federation.venue` record to populate the generated rounds and linked matches.\n\nTesting and coverage\n\nAdd unit and integration tests covering the following:\n\n- `federation.stage.progression`: ensure `action_execute()` selects the correct teams across single-group and cross-group rules and that `seeding_method` options behave as documented.\n- `federation.tournament.template`: applying a template creates the expected stages, groups and progression rules.\n- Round-robin scheduling: `rounds_count`, `schedule_by_round`, automatic round materialisation, alternation of male/female fixtures, and repeat cycles.\n- Knockout bracket generation: bracket size determination, bye handling, and automatic wiring of placeholder matches and advancement on `action_done()`.\n- Round constraints: enforce no duplicate same-category pairings inside the same round.\n\n## Architecture and conventions\n\nThis technical note documents architecture, coding conventions, workflows, and extension points for the Sports Federation Odoo 19 custom addons collection located in the `odoo/` folder. It is intended for developers, integrators, and release engineers working on federation features: tournaments, matches, rosters, refereeing, results pipelines, and public website publication.\n\n### Shared workflow state helpers (2026-04-18)\n\nWhere one addon reuses the same workflow vocabulary across multiple models,\nkeep the selection tuples and state-role predicates in a small plain Python\nhelper module instead of repeating raw string tuples in each model.\n\n- `sports_federation_import_tools/workflow_states.py` now owns the inbound\n    delivery and import-governance lifecycle constants used by the delivery\n    model, governance job model, wizard mixin, migration backfill, and tests.\n- `sports_federation_governance/workflow_states.py` now owns the override\n    request and decision lifecycle constants used by the request, decision,\n    outcome, and test modules.\n- When new logic only needs to know the semantic role of a state, prefer a\n    helper predicate such as `is_import_job_approved(...)` over direct string\n    comparisons so future state changes stay localized.\n\n## Table of contents\n\n- Executive summary\n- High-level architecture and module responsibilities\n- Data model conventions and patterns\n- Workflows and state machines (tournament lifecycle, match-day, result pipeline)\n- Competition engine — algorithms, wizards, and deterministic behaviours\n- Controllers, portal, and public site patterns\n- Security model and record rules\n- Performance, scaling and operational concerns\n- Testing, CI and quality gates\n- Upgrade, migrations and deployment notes\n- Developer workflow: how to add models, wizards, views, and tests\n- Examples and reference snippets\n\n## Executive summary\n\nThe project is a modular suite of Odoo 19 addons implementing a sports federation management system. Modules are intentionally small and focused: `sports_federation_base` owns master data (clubs, teams, seasons), `sports_federation_tournament` implements tournament structure and match records, and the competition addons own registration, format, calendar, scheduling, approval, and match-day operations. Domain features (`people`, `rosters`, `officiating`, `result_control`, `standings`, `public_site`, `notifications`, `reporting`) extend core behaviour without mixing responsibilities.\n\nDesign goals\n\n- Keep modules decoupled and installable independently where practical.\n- Encode business logic in computed models and service/wizard classes rather than ad-hoc scripts.\n- Enforce separation of duties via groups and record rules (submit/verify/approve in the result pipeline).\n- Make scheduling deterministic and testable (repeatable outputs from the same inputs).\n\n## High-level architecture and module responsibilities\n\n- `sports_federation_base` — Master data: `federation.club`, `federation.team`, `federation.season`, `federation.season.registration`. Ownership of base security groups and global menus. Holds common `ir.sequence` definitions.\n- `sports_federation_tournament` — Tournament structure: `federation.competition`, `federation.tournament`, `federation.tournament.stage`, `federation.group`, `federation.tournament.participant`, and `federation.match`. Implements match lifecycle and basic match behaviour.\n- `sports_federation_format` and `sports_federation_scheduling` — Structure generation, deterministic fixture assignment, validation, and fairness services. Keep algorithmic code stateless and place transient entrypoints in the owning module's `wizards/` package.\n- `sports_federation_people` — Player and license models used for eligibility checks and rosters.\n- `sports_federation_rosters` — Season rosters and match sheet management.\n- `sports_federation_officiating` — Referee registry and assignment workflows.\n- `sports_federation_finance_bridge` — Lightweight finance events with source-linked,\n  idempotent hooks for registrations, result approval, sanctions, officiating,\n  and venue settlements.\n- `sports_federation_notifications` — Central email/activity dispatcher and\n    audit log for registration, publication, result, officiating, standings, and\n    finance workflow events.\n- `sports_federation_result_control` — Result submission, verification, approval, contest and correction flows.\n- `sports_federation_standings` — Standings computation, tie-break logic, and publishing controls.\n- `sports_federation_public_site` / `sports_federation_portal` — Website and portal layers for public pages and club self-service.\n\nInter-module rules\n\n- Use `depends` in `__manifest__.py` for compile-time coupling and prefer runtime loose coupling in service code.\n- Avoid importing models directly across modules in shared utils; reference them through the ORM (`env['federation.model']`).\n\nSecurity-group compatibility\n\n- Odoo 19 classifies application groups through `res.groups.privilege` records. Addons must assign a group with `privilege_id`; `category_id` belongs on the privilege and is no longer a valid field on `res.groups`.\n- Federation privileges should reference an existing module category such as `base.module_category_services` and remain in the addon security XML beside the groups they classify. This preserves the access-rights UI grouping without relying on the removed pre-Odoo-19 group field.\n\n## Data model conventions and patterns\n\n- Names: all domain models use the `federation.` prefix.\n- Fields: prefer explicit names (`home_score`, `away_score`, `match_date`, `venue_id`). Use `_id` for Many2one fields.\n- Sequences: centralize `ir.sequence` definitions under the modules that issue numbers (licenses, registrations, match references).\n- States: encode lifecycle using `state` selection fields. Implement transition methods (e.g., `action_confirm()`) that include invariant checks and post-transition side-effects (message_post, cron triggers).\n- Constraints and indexes: use `_sql_constraints` for DB-level uniqueness and `index=True` on frequently filtered fields.\n\nORM best practices\n\n- Use `@api.depends` for computed fields; mark heavy computed fields with `store=True` when the value is frequently filtered or sorted.\n- Use `read_group` for group-by aggregations instead of computing aggregates in Python loops.\n- When creating many records (e.g., fixtures for a large tournament), batch creations in transactions and avoid per-record flushes where possible.\n\n## Workflows and state machines\n\nThe canonical workflows live in `odoo/_workflows` (authoritative). Implementation notes below reflect the codebase expectations.\n\nTournament lifecycle\n\n- States: `draft → open → in_progress → closed | cancelled`.\n- Preconditions for `open`: participants registered/confirmed, ruleset assigned, optional venues configured.\n- Schedule creation typically moves the tournament to `in_progress` (explicit action required).\n- Archive and restore are explicit backend actions. Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before archiving, and only active draft tournaments linked to a season may be opened.\n\nMatch lifecycle and match-day operations\n\n- States: `draft → scheduled → in_progress → done | cancelled`.\n- Pre-match checks: both teams have confirmed match-sheets, required referee roles filled and confirmed, no suspensions on selected players, venue confirmed.\n- Officiating readiness is computed directly on the match from assignment state, rule-set referee counts, overdue confirmations, and referee certification validity so operators can filter or inspect staffing gaps without opening each assignment.\n- During match: record events (substitutions, cards) which feed the discipline and finance modules.\n\nResult pipeline\n\n- States: `not_submitted → submitted → verified → approved` (exceptions: `contested`, `corrected`).\n- Permissions: separate groups for submit/verify/approve to enforce audit and separation of duties.\n- Approved results are the only ones included in official standings computations.\n- The same user must not submit, verify, and approve the same result. Self-verification is blocked and approvers cannot approve their own submissions or the result they verified.\n- Approving, contesting, correcting, or resetting a result triggers automatic recomputation of linked non-frozen standings. Approved scores become immutable until the result is moved out of the approved state.\n\n## Competition engine — algorithms and wizards\n\nPrinciples\n\n- Determinism: given the same input (participant list, seeding, start datetime) the schedule generation must produce the same fixtures. Sort input participants by an unambiguous key (id or explicit seeding) before generation.\n- Testability: isolate algorithms in service classes and unit-test them with small deterministic datasets.\n\nRound-robin (circle method)\n\n- Supports odd/even participant counts (auto bye round for odd counts) and single/double round-robin.\n- Complexity: O(n^2) matches for n participants (n*(n-1)/2 for single round-robin).\n\nExample pseudocode (circle method)\n\n```python\ndef generate_round_robin(participants, double=False):\n    participants = sorted(participants, key=lambda p: p.seeding or p.id)\n    if len(participants) % 2 == 1:\n        participants.append(None)  # bye\n    n = len(participants)\n    rounds = []\n    for r in range(n - 1):\n        pairs = []\n        for i in range(n // 2):\n            a = participants[i]\n            b = participants[n - 1 - i]\n            if a is not None and b is not None:\n                pairs.append((a, b))\n        rounds.append(pairs)\n        participants = [participants[0]] + participants[-1:] + participants[1:-1]\n    if double:\n        return rounds + [reverse_pairs(r) for r in rounds]\n    return rounds\n```\n\nKnockout bracket generation\n\n- Seeding strategies: `natural` (order of participants) and `power_of_two` (map to nearest bracket size and set byes).\n- Ensure bracket seeding is deterministic and documented in the UI.\n\nWizards\n\n- Wizards (transient models under `wizards/`) do validations, produce a `summary` preview, and require explicit confirmation to persist matches. They must not perform destructive replacements unless the user explicitly enables `overwrite`.\n- Competition-generation wizards validate tournament state, the effective rule set, minimum participant counts, and stage/group ownership before creating matches. Overwrite mode is warning-first and should remain opt-in.\n\n## Controllers, portal, and public site patterns\n\nPortal patterns\n\n- Use a dedicated `federation.club.representative` model to map `res.users` → `federation.club` for portal ownership and record rules.\n- Controllers must perform ownership validation (`_get_clubs_for_user()`) before writes. Record rules are enforcement, controllers are defense-in-depth.\n- ORM-level ownership constraints should mirror controller checks for portal-created registrations so bypassing a controller does not widen access.\n- The tournament operations board (`/sports/competitions/<edition-slug>/operations`) extends these patterns with an Owl frontend. Portal access requires provable tournament-scoped activity (registration, participant, or visible match). Writes delegate to existing result-control action methods. The Owl app uses standalone `mount()` from `@odoo/owl`, not the backend webclient `mountComponent`, since it runs inside the website/portal frontend context. It mounts immediately so the board can render its own loading and error states, applies a 30-second timeout to the first payload fetch, and relies on a server-side payload that includes ranked action-queue rows, court summaries, next-step hints, and schedule labels so the browser stays presentation-focused.\n\nPublic site\n\n- Public controllers use `auth='public'` and `sudo()` for reads. Only expose non-sensitive fields (no emails/phones/notes) to public templates.\n- Enforce `website_published` and the relevant visibility toggle (`show_public_results`, `show_public_standings`) before serving direct public routes.\n- When a controller must deny a hidden portal or public route with 404, raise the HTTP exception (`raise request.not_found()`) instead of returning it, so fail-closed paths stay quiet in logs and match Odoo's expected flow.\n- Render public rich text through sanitized website field rendering rather than raw `t-raw` output.\n- Keep `public_slug` unique even while the public routes remain model-bound, so publication metadata and future external references cannot collide.\n\nCSRF and forms\n\n- All POST forms must include `csrf_token` and controllers must validate it.\n\n## Security model and record rules\n\nKey principles\n\n- Least privilege: create narrowly-scoped groups and map CRUD rights in `security/ir.model.access.csv`.\n- Record rules: express row-level ownership using domains (e.g., `('club_id','in', user.representative_ids.mapped('club_id').ids)`).\n- Avoid uncontrolled `sudo()` on write operations.\n\nGroups and separation of duties\n\n- Federation Staff (submit results)\n- Result Verifier (verify submitted results)\n- Result Approver (approve verified results)\n- Referee Coordinator (assign referees)\n- Portal Club Representative (portal users)\n\n## Performance, scaling and operational concerns\n\nLarge tournaments and match volumes\n\n- Match generation: create matches in batches using `create()` on list-of-dicts to minimize ORM overhead. Consider raw SQL insert for extremely large volumes but keep referential integrity and Odoo cache considerations in mind.\n- Indexes: ensure `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `group_id`, `match_date`, and `state` fields are indexed.\n- Aggregation: compute standings incrementally or via nightly cron for large datasets. Prefer `read_group` for real-time small aggregate queries.\n\nBackground and asynchronous work\n\n- Use `ir.cron` for scheduled recomputes. For heavy parallel work consider `queue_job` or an external worker queue.\n\nMemory and worker tuning\n\n- For large batch jobs run them on a dedicated worker with increased memory limits and tuned `limit_time_cpu` and `limit_time_real` values.\n\n## Testing, CI and quality gates\n\nTest types\n\n- Unit tests: service classes and algorithms (no DB or minimal mock DB). Keep these fast and deterministic.\n- Integration tests: Odoo testcases exercising ORM-level behaviour and workflows.\n- Functional tests: simulate portal and public flows (controller-level) when needed.\n\nCI recommendations\n\n- Run module tests in CI and fail PRs on test regressions.\n- Include a lint step (flake8/black for Python where applicable) and XML/manifest validation.\n- The repository CI entrypoint is `ci/run_tests.sh`; the GitHub workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reuses that script and runs Black/Flake8 from `requirements.txt`.\n- `ci/run_tests.sh` also provides named suites (`competition_core`, `portal_public_ops`, `finance_reporting`) so maintainers can run the same focused coverage locally and in GitHub Actions.\n- The runner supports a frontend-only mode (`--frontend-module`) that performs XML/QWeb parsing, JavaScript syntax and QUnit-registration checks, asset checks, portal accessibility/mobile checks, and selected HTTP tests without scheduling or standings suites.\n- `--affected-from <ref> --include-dependents` resolves changed addons from git and expands their manifest reverse-dependency closure before testing.\n- Each run retains `test_failures.log`, `expected_diagnostics.log`, `infrastructure.log`, and `full.log`; `--keep-on-failure` additionally preserves runtime artifacts and writes exact inspection commands.\n- Public-site, portal, and reporting performance hotspots should carry explicit `assertQueryCount(...)` budgets in their regression suites; the current enforced budgets are summarized in `TESTING_GUIDE.md`.\n- Do not commit runtime credentials. Keep local CI values in `ci/.env`, commit only `ci/.env.example`, and let CI generate ephemeral values at runtime.\n- Integration environment variables: maintain `ci/integrations.env.example` with the common external-integration keys (SMTP, SendGrid/Mailgun keys, OAuth client IDs/secrets, Slack webhook, Twilio credentials, AWS S3 keys). Keep real values out of VCS and populate `ci/.env` locally or via your secret store in CI runs.\n- Contributor-facing local setup, suite selection, and script validation commands live in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nExample test command\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n```\n\n## Upgrade, migrations and deployment notes\n\nManifest and data maintenance\n\n- Keep `__manifest__.py` `version` and `data` accurate. Prefer small, focused upgrade scripts to large one-off DB migrations.\n- For breaking model changes provide a dedicated migration script (`openupgrade` style) and document steps.\n- `ci/check_migration_review.py` should pass whenever model, view, or controller ownership changes are present. Keep hooks idempotent and well-tested.\n\nBackups and rollback\n\n- Always perform full DB and filestore backups prior to upgrades. Test restore paths in your staging environment.\n\n## Developer workflow: add/modify checklist\n\nArchitecture decisions\n\n- Repository-level architectural choices that cut across portal trust\n    boundaries, reporting SQL views, or public route ownership live in `adr/`.\n- Update the relevant ADR in the same change set when one of those core\n    decisions materially changes.\n\nWhen introducing a new feature follow this minimal patch checklist:\n\n1. A query-count increase is a regression unless the test and the\nbudget are updated together with a reason.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Test Taxonomy\n\nThe project uses three test classes depending on what is being tested:\n\n### `TransactionCase` — ORM-level unit and integration tests\n\nUsed for: model methods, computed fields, `@api.constrains` validators,\nwizards, services, and controller methods that are tested by injecting a mock\n\nEach test runs inside a savepoint that is rolled back after the test, so data\n\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n        cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\n            \"name\": \"Test Club\",\n            \"code\": \"TC01\",\n        })\n\n    def test_code_must_be_unique(self):\n        with self.assertRaises(Exception):\n            self.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\"name\": \"Dup\", \"code\": \"TC01\"})\n            self.env.cr.flush()\n```\n\n**Put shared fixtures in `setUpClass`.** Fixtures created there are shared\nacross all test methods (and rolled back as a unit at the end of the class).\nFixtures created inside individual test methods are rolled back after each\nmethod.\n### `HttpCase` — end-to-end HTTP smoke tests\n\nUsed for: verifying that routes return the expected HTTP status code, CSRF\ntoken handling, portal login flows.\n\nRequires a real database and a running Odoo HTTP server. These tests must be\ntagged `@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\")` so they run after all modules\nare loaded.\n\n```python\nfrom odoo.tests.common import HttpCase, tagged\n\n@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\")\nclass TestPublicSiteHttpSmoke(HttpCase):\n    def test_tournaments_list_returns_200(self):\n        response = self.url_open(\"/competitions\")\n        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)\n```\n\nHTTP tests are significantly slower than `TransactionCase` tests and require\n`sports_federation_portal` to be installed. Use the\n`unittest.SkipTest` pattern to skip gracefully when optional modules are absent:\n\n```python\n@classmethod\ndef setUpClass(cls):\n    super().setUpClass()\n    with cls.registry.cursor() as cr:\n        env = api.Environment(cr, SUPERUSER_ID, {})\n        if not env.ref(\"sports_federation_portal.group_federation_portal_club\",\n                       raise_if_not_found=False):\n            raise unittest.SkipTest(\"sports_federation_portal not installed\")\n```\n\n### `TransactionCase` with a mock `request` — controller unit tests\n\nUsed for: testing controller methods that call `request.env` without running an\nHTTP server. Inject a `SimpleNamespace` as the request stub and patch the\n`request` module attribute.\n\n```python\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\nfrom unittest.mock import patch\n\nclass TestCompetitionsApiJson(TransactionCase):\n\n    def test_rate_limit_blocks_after_limit(self):\n        request_stub = SimpleNamespace(\n            env=self.env,\n            httprequest=SimpleNamespace(remote_addr=\"198.51.100.1\", headers={}),\n        )\n        controller = PublicTournamentHubController()\n        with patch(\n            \"odoo.addons.sports_federation_public_site\"\n            \".controllers.public_competitions.request\",\n            request_stub,\n        ):\n            result = controller.competitions_api_json()\n        self.assertIn(\"tournaments\", result)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Shared Fixture Patterns\n\n### Basic club/team/season fixture\n\nThis fixture appears in almost every module's test. Copy it as a starting point\nrather than re-inventing it.\n\n```python\n@classmethod\ndef setUpClass(cls):\n    super().setUpClass()\n    cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Fixture Club\", \"code\": \"FXC\",\n    })\n    cls.team_a = cls.env[\"federation.team\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Team A\", \"club_id\": cls.club.id, \"code\": \"TFA\",\n    })\n    cls.team_b = cls.env[\"federation.team\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Team B\", \"club_id\": cls.club.id, \"code\": \"TFB\",\n    })\n    cls.season = cls.env[\"federation.season\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Test Season\",\n        \"code\": \"TS26\",\n        \"date_start\": \"2026-01-01\",\n        \"date_end\": \"2026-12-31\",\n    })\n    cls.tournament = cls.env[\"federation.tournament\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Test Tournament\",\n        \"code\": \"TT26\",\n        \"season_id\": cls.season.id,\n        \"date_start\": \"2026-06-01\",\n        \"state\": \"open\",\n    })\n```\n\n### Portal ownership fixture\n\nWhen testing portal access, create users with the portal club group and link\nthem to a club via `federation.club.representative`. This pattern is used\nthroughout `sports_federation_portal/tests/`.\n\n```python\nfrom odoo import SUPERUSER_ID, api\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\nclass TestPortalOwnership(TransactionCase):\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n        cls.portal_group = cls.env.ref(\n            \"sports_federation_portal.group_federation_portal_club\"\n        )\n        cls.club_a = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Portal Club A\", \"code\": \"PCA\"}\n        )\n        cls.club_b = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Portal Club B\", \"code\": \"PCB\"}\n        )\n\n        def _make_user(name, login):\n                cls.env[\"res.users\"]\n                .with_context(no_reset_password=True)\n                .create({\n                    \"login\": login,\n            )\n        cls.user_a = _make_user(\"User A\", \"usera@example.com\")\n\n\n## Maintained performance budgets\n\nThese are the current CI budgets for the most sensitive read paths:\n\n| Path | Budget |\n|---|---:|\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_featured_tournaments(limit=4)` | 1 query |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_live_tournaments(limit=4)` | 1 query |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_recent_result_tournaments(limit=4)` | 3 queries |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_schedule_sections()` | 4 queries |\n| `federation.team.roster.line._portal_get_available_players()` | 7 queries |\n| `federation.report.schedule._build_season_portfolio_rows()` | 3 queries |\n| `federation.report.schedule._build_club_performance_rows()` | 4 queries |\n| `federation.report.snapshot._compliance_pending_total()` | 1 aggregate query |\n| scheduling validation smoke | ≤ 25 seconds |\n\nThe authoritative tests are in the competition, public-site, portal,\nreporting, and domain test suites.
