+{"content": "# Testing Guide\n\nLast updated: 2026-09-02\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\n\nThis guide explains the project's test taxonomy, how to write tests for each\ncategory, and how to keep query-budget assertions current.\n\nPerformance budgets and explain snapshots are maintained here with the test\npatterns below. A query-count increase is a regression unless the test and the\nbudget are updated together with a reason.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Test Taxonomy\n\nThe project uses three test classes depending on what is being tested:\n\n### `TransactionCase` — ORM-level unit and integration tests\n\nUsed for: model methods, computed fields, `@api.constrains` validators,\nwizards, services, and controller methods that are tested by injecting a mock\n\nEach test runs inside a savepoint that is rolled back after the test, so data\n\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n        cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\n            \"name\": \"Test Club\",\n            \"code\": \"TC01\",\n        })\n\n    def test_code_must_be_unique(self):\n        with self.assertRaises(Exception):\n            self.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\"name\": \"Dup\", \"code\": \"TC01\"})\n            self.env.cr.flush()\n```\n\n**Put shared fixtures in `setUpClass`.** Fixtures created there are shared\nacross all test methods (and rolled back as a unit at the end of the class).\nFixtures created inside individual test methods are rolled back after each\nmethod.\n### `HttpCase` — end-to-end HTTP smoke tests\n\nUsed for: verifying that routes return the expected HTTP status code, CSRF\ntoken handling, portal login flows.\n\nRequires a real database and a running Odoo HTTP server. These tests must be\ntagged `@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\")` so they run after all modules\nare loaded.\n\n```python\nfrom odoo.tests.common import HttpCase, tagged\n\n@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\")\nclass TestPublicSiteHttpSmoke(HttpCase):\n    def test_tournaments_list_returns_200(self):\n        response = self.url_open(\"/competitions\")\n        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)\n```\n\nHTTP tests are significantly slower than `TransactionCase` tests and require\n`sports_federation_portal` to be installed. Use the\n`unittest.SkipTest` pattern to skip gracefully when optional modules are absent:\n\n```python\n@classmethod\ndef setUpClass(cls):\n    super().setUpClass()\n    with cls.registry.cursor() as cr:\n        env = api.Environment(cr, SUPERUSER_ID, {})\n        if not env.ref(\"sports_federation_portal.group_federation_portal_club\",\n                       raise_if_not_found=False):\n            raise unittest.SkipTest(\"sports_federation_portal not installed\")\n```\n\n### `TransactionCase` with a mock `request` — controller unit tests\n\nUsed for: testing controller methods that call `request.env` without running an\nHTTP server. Inject a `SimpleNamespace` as the request stub and patch the\n`request` module attribute.\n\n```python\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\nfrom unittest.mock import patch\n\nclass TestCompetitionsApiJson(TransactionCase):\n\n    def test_rate_limit_blocks_after_limit(self):\n        request_stub = SimpleNamespace(\n            env=self.env,\n            httprequest=SimpleNamespace(remote_addr=\"198.51.100.1\", headers={}),\n        )\n        controller = PublicTournamentHubController()\n        with patch(\n            \"odoo.addons.sports_federation_public_site\"\n            \".controllers.public_competitions.request\",\n            request_stub,\n        ):\n            result = controller.competitions_api_json()\n        self.assertIn(\"tournaments\", result)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Shared Fixture Patterns\n\n### Basic club/team/season fixture\n\nThis fixture appears in almost every module's test. Copy it as a starting point\nrather than re-inventing it.\n\n```python\n@classmethod\ndef setUpClass(cls):\n    super().setUpClass()\n    cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Fixture Club\", \"code\": \"FXC\",\n    })\n    cls.team_a = cls.env[\"federation.team\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Team A\", \"club_id\": cls.club.id, \"code\": \"TFA\",\n    })\n    cls.team_b = cls.env[\"federation.team\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Team B\", \"club_id\": cls.club.id, \"code\": \"TFB\",\n    })\n    cls.season = cls.env[\"federation.season\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Test Season\",\n        \"code\": \"TS26\",\n        \"date_start\": \"2026-01-01\",\n        \"date_end\": \"2026-12-31\",\n    })\n    cls.tournament = cls.env[\"federation.tournament\"].create({\n        \"name\": \"Test Tournament\",\n        \"code\": \"TT26\",\n        \"season_id\": cls.season.id,\n        \"date_start\": \"2026-06-01\",\n        \"state\": \"open\",\n    })\n```\n\n### Portal ownership fixture\n\nWhen testing portal access, create users with the portal club group and link\nthem to a club via `federation.club.representative`. This pattern is used\nthroughout `sports_federation_portal/tests/`.\n\n```python\nfrom odoo import SUPERUSER_ID, api\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\nclass TestPortalOwnership(TransactionCase):\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n        cls.portal_group = cls.env.ref(\n            \"sports_federation_portal.group_federation_portal_club\"\n        )\n        cls.club_a = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Portal Club A\", \"code\": \"PCA\"}\n        )\n        cls.club_b = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Portal Club B\", \"code\": \"PCB\"}\n        )\n\n        def _make_user(name, login):\n                cls.env[\"res.users\"]\n                .with_context(no_reset_password=True)\n                .create({\n                    \"login\": login,\n            )\n        cls.user_a = _make_user(\"User A\", \"usera@example.com\")\n\n\n## Maintained performance budgets\n\nThese are the current CI budgets for the most sensitive read paths:\n\n| Path | Budget |\n|---|---:|\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_featured_tournaments(limit=4)` | 1 query |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_live_tournaments(limit=4)` | 1 query |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_recent_result_tournaments(limit=4)` | 3 queries |\n| `federation.tournament.get_public_schedule_sections()` | 4 queries |\n| `federation.team.roster.line._portal_get_available_players()` | 7 queries |\n| `federation.report.schedule._build_season_portfolio_rows()` | 3 queries |\n| `federation.report.schedule._build_club_performance_rows()` | 4 queries |\n| `federation.report.snapshot._compliance_pending_total()` | 1 aggregate query |\n| scheduling validation smoke | ≤ 25 seconds |\n\nThe authoritative tests are in the competition, public-site, portal,\nreporting, and domain test suites. Scheduling regressions belong in\n`sports_federation_scheduling/tests/` and calendar regressions belong in\n`sports_federation_calendar/tests/`.\nWhen a budget changes, update the assertion, explain the cause, and review the\ncorresponding SQL plan or index before changing the documented value.\n        # Link users to clubs via representative records\n        for user, club in ((cls.user_a, cls.club_a), (cls.user_b, cls.club_b)):\n            cls.env[\"federation.club.representative\"].create({\n                \"club_id\": club.id,\n                \"user_id\": user.id,\n                \"role_type_id\": cls.env.ref(\n                    \"sports_federation_portal.role_type_competition_contact\"\n                ).id,\n            })\n\n    def test_club_a_cannot_see_club_b_roster(self):\n        \"\"\"Portal user A must not be able to reach a roster belonging to club B.\"\"\"\n        privilege = self.env[\"federation.portal.privilege\"]\n        with self.assertRaises(AccessError):\n            privilege.with_user(self.user_a).portal_search_by_id(\n                \"federation.team.roster\",\n                self.club_b_roster.id,\n            )\n```\n\nSee `sports_federation_portal/tests/test_portal_ownership_guard.py` for a\ncomplete working example.\n\n### Frozen-time fixture for time-sensitive logic\n\nFor rate limiting, deadlines, and scheduling logic, freeze time with\n`unittest.mock.patch.object`:\n\n```python\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom unittest.mock import patch\n\ndef test_consume_blocks_after_limit(self):\n    service = self.env[\"federation.request.rate.limit\"].sudo()\n    frozen_time = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 12, 0, 0)\n    with patch.object(type(service), \"_get_now\", return_value=frozen_time):\n        first = service.consume(\"public_competitions_json\", \"ip:10.0.0.1\")\n        second = service.consume(\"public_competitions_json\", \"ip:10.0.0.1\")\n    self.assertTrue(first[\"allowed\"])\n    self.assertFalse(second[\"allowed\"])  # limit is 1 in this test\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Query-Count Budgets\n\nSeveral test suites assert exact query counts to catch N+1 regressions:\n\n```python\ndef test_public_discovery_helpers_stay_within_query_budget(self):\n    with self.assertQueryCount(1):\n        featured = self.env[\"federation.tournament\"].get_public_featured_tournaments(limit=4)\n    with self.assertQueryCount(3):\n        recent = self.env[\"federation.tournament\"].get_public_recent_result_tournaments(limit=4)\n```\n\n**Rules:**\n- `assertQueryCount(N)` fails if the block executes more or fewer than `N`\n  queries. Fewer queries is also a failure because it may indicate a test\n  regression (e.g., empty dataset masking missing queries).\n- Budgets live in the maintained performance section of this guide. If you\n    lower a budget, update that section.\n- If your change legitimately increases a query count, update the assertion\n    and add a comment explaining why, and update the budget table in this guide.\n\n---\n\n## 4. EXPLAIN Snapshot Tests\n\nFor critical query paths, the CI runs `ci/check_explain_snapshots.py`, which\ncompares `EXPLAIN` output against stored snapshots in `ci/explain_snapshots/`.\n\nTo add a new snapshot:\n\n```bash\n# Connect to the CI database and run EXPLAIN\ndocker compose exec db psql -U odoo -d odoo_ci_test -c \\\n  \"EXPLAIN SELECT ... FROM federation_tournament WHERE ...\"\n# Save the output to ci/explain_snapshots/<descriptive_name>.txt\n```\n\nA snapshot regression (e.g., a sequential scan replacing an index scan) fails\nCI. Review the output, add the necessary index, or update the snapshot with\na comment explaining the regression is acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What to Test for Each Change Type\n\n| Change type | Required test |\n|---|---|\n| New model field | `test_<model>_<field>_<rule>` validating the constraint or default |\n| New `@api.constrains` | One passing case + one failing case |\n| New computed field | Verify the value before and after the triggering field changes |\n| New wizard | End-to-end test: create input records → call wizard → assert output records (counts, states) |\n| New controller route | Either an HTTP smoke test (200/404) or a mock-request unit test |\n| Portal write | Always add a cross-club access-denial test in addition to the happy path |\n| Standings / schedule logic | `assertQueryCount` + correctness assertion for a minimal dataset |\n| Rate limiting | Frozen-time test: N requests pass, N+1 is blocked; verify `Retry-After` header |\n\n---\n\n## 6. Running Tests in CI\n\n```bash\n# Run the suite that covers your changed module\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Run just one module (faster when iterating)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings\n\n# Run participant readiness discovery guard (fails if post-tests are not discovered)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite rosters_readiness_guard\n\n# Equivalent explicit form when you need direct control\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_rosters --test-tags sf_rosters_participant_readiness --require-post-tests 1\n\n# Skip browser bootstrap when the run has no HttpCase/browser coverage\nCI_SKIP_BROWSER_BOOTSTRAP=1 bash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Frontend-only feedback loop: portal accessibility/mobile templates and\n# selected HTTP rendering tests\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --frontend-module sports_federation_portal\n\n# Detect changed addons and expand to all manifest reverse dependents\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --affected-from origin/main --include-dependents\n\n# Retain failed containers, database, filestore, generated config, and commands\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_portal --keep-on-failure\n\n# Run all suites (used in final PR validation)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh\n```\n\nThe CI runner produces a results block at the end:\n\n```\n\nEvery run also writes `test_failures.log`, `expected_diagnostics.log`,\n`infrastructure.log`, and `full.log` under `ci/logs/<timestamp>/`. A failed\n`--keep-on-failure` run writes `retained-container-commands.sh` with exact\ninspection and cleanup commands; successful runs clean up automatically.\n════════════════════════════════\n  RESULTS\n════════════════════════════════\n  Exit code:     0\n  Tests run:     62\n  Tests passed:  62\n  Tests failed:  0\n  Test errors:   0\n════════════════════════════════\n```\n\nA non-zero exit code means the CI gate failed. Check the container logs for\nthe failing test name and traceback:\n\n```bash\ndocker logs <container-name> 2>&1 | grep -A 20 \"FAIL\\|ERROR\"\n```\n\n### Discovery-safe tag convention\n\nFor high-risk regression suites, add an explicit class-level tag in addition to the usual install timing tags:\n\n```python\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase, tagged\n\n@tagged(\"-at_install\", \"post_install\", \"sf_<module>_<feature>\")\nclass TestFeature(TransactionCase):\n    ...\n```\n\nUse lowercase snake-case tags prefixed with `sf_` (example: `sf_rosters_participant_readiness`).\nThis enables deterministic CI selection and allows `--require-post-tests` gating to detect discovery regressions early.\n\n### Critical suite registry\n\nThe CI runner enforces a minimum discovered post-test count for critical suites.\nThis prevents false-green runs where discovery is broken and no tests execute.\n\nGitHub Actions now also runs a dedicated integration matrix lane for\n`people_rosters_rules` and `ops_and_notifications` so cross-module behavior is\nvalidated on every push and pull request.\n\n| Suite | Default minimum post-tests | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `competition_core` | 1 | Core workflow sanity gate |\n| `portal_public_ops` | 1 | Portal/public ownership and route guard |\n| `finance_reporting` | 1 | Finance and reporting guard |\n| `release_surfaces` | 1 | Broad release surface guard |\n| `people_rosters_rules` | 1 | Domain rules and roster workflow guard |\n| `ops_and_notifications` | 1 | Operations and notification guard |\n| `rosters_readiness_guard` | 1 | Explicit tag `sf_rosters_participant_readiness` |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Test File Conventions\n\n- One test file per logical area in `tests/` (e.g., `test_round_robin.py`,\n  `test_knockout.py` — not one giant `test_all.py`).\n- File names: `test_<noun>.py` (noun = model name, workflow name, or feature).\n- Class name: `Test<Topic>` (e.g., `TestRoundRobin`, `TestPortalOwnershipGuard`).\n- `setUpClass` creates shared fixtures; individual test methods create only what\n  they uniquely need.\n- Test method names: `test_<what>_<expected_outcome>` (e.g.,\n  `test_duplicate_code_raises_validation_error`).\n- Register new test files in `tests/__init__.py` with `from . import test_myfile`.\n\n\n## Release performance qualification\n\nThe release-candidate pipeline runs the maintained query-budget lane after the core, portal, and public qualification lanes:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh performance\n```\n\nThe versioned registry is `ci/performance_budgets.json`. The contract checker verifies the exact targeted test classes, preventing a renamed class from silently turning the lane into an empty run. Budget increases require measured evidence in `RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md`. Synthetic data must be identified as synthetic.\n\n## Release baseline qualification\n\nAfter committing the candidate and confirming that no tracked changes remain,\nrun the complete baseline gate:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_release_baseline.sh\n```\n\nThis wraps the authoritative RC lanes and records lane evidence under\n`artifacts/release/baseline/`. A lane failure records failed evidence before the\nscript exits. Odoo is executed from the pinned `odoo:19` image through\n`ci/docker-compose.ci.yaml`; a single retained Compose project carries the\nfresh-install database through the focused lanes and the separate upgrade\ndatabase through the same-version upgrade lane. The runner removes that\nproject on exit while preserving the evidence directory. To clean an\ninterrupted run manually, use:\n\n```bash\nRC_COMPOSE_PROJECT=sf_rc_<project> scripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh cleanup\n```\n\nDo not use this wrapper to hide or bypass individual RC failures.\n\n\n## Migration and rollback qualification\n\nThe release migration rehearsal uses versioned invariants from\n`ci/release_invariants.json` and runs role-separated acceptance against the\nupgraded database:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh acceptance\nscripts/ci/run_migration_rehearsal.sh --help\n```\n\nKeep invariant names stable once evidence has been archived. Add a count or\nintegrity check when a new release-critical ownership boundary is introduced.\nDo not remove a check merely to accommodate unexplained migration drift.\n", "content_length": 17049, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "modified", "path": "TESTING_GUIDE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c23ac295569262ec89ea8c406f5936f14feb4c75b19663f63f6c0eeba6c4747", "size_bytes": 17255}
 {"content": "# Troubleshooting Guide\n\nLast updated: 2026-05-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nReview cadence: Every release train\n\nThis guide documents known issues, their root causes, and the recommended\nrecovery steps. Always check this file before escalating to a developer.\n\n---\n\n## Quick Diagnostic Checklist\n\nBefore diving into a specific symptom, run these checks first:\n\n```bash\n# 1. All containers running?\ndocker compose ps\n\n# 2. Any Python errors in the Odoo log?\ndocker compose logs odoo 2>&1 | grep -i \"error\\|traceback\\|exception\" | tail -20\n\n# 3. PostgreSQL accepting connections?\ndocker compose exec db pg_isready -U odoo\n\n# 4. Scheduled actions healthy?\n# Check in the back office: Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions\n# Look for any action where \"Last Execution\" shows a failure icon.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Symptom Index\n\n| Symptom | Section |\n|---|---|\n| Match form crashes with `UndefinedColumn` | [§1](#1-match-form-crashes-with-undefinedcolumn) |\n| Standings not recomputing after result approval | [§2](#2-standings-not-recomputing-after-result-approval) |\n| Notifications not sending | [§3](#3-notifications-not-sending) |\n| Import wizard dry-run always fails | [§4](#4-import-wizard-dry-run-always-fails) |\n| Rate limit buckets never cleared | [§5](#5-rate-limit-buckets-never-cleared) |\n| CI container fails to start PostgreSQL | [§6](#6-ci-container-fails-to-start-postgresql) |\n| Portal page shows 403 / `AccessError` | [§7](#7-portal-page-shows-403--accesserror) |\n| Public JSON feed returns `500` | [§8](#8-public-json-feed-returns-500) |\n| Player shows `is_eligible = False` after license activation | [§9](#9-player-shows-is_eligible--false-after-license-activation) |\n| Finance events not exporting to partner | [§10](#10-finance-events-not-exporting-to-partner) |\n| Reporting schedule stuck in `running` | [§11](#11-reporting-schedule-stuck-in-running) |\n| Roster assignment_ready False with no clear reason | [§12](#12-roster-assignment_ready-false-with-no-clear-reason) |\n\n---\n\n## 1. Match Form Crashes with `UndefinedColumn`\n\n**Symptom**: Opening or saving a match record raises a `ProgrammingError:\ncolumn \"xyz\" of relation \"federation_match\" does not exist`.\n\n**Cause**: A `store=True` computed field was added to the match model in a\nnew release but the database column was never created because the module was\nnot upgraded after the code change.\n\n**Fix**:\n\n```bash\n# Upgrade the affected module(s) to create the missing column\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo \\\n  -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf \\\n  -d odoo \\\n  -u sports_federation_tournament,sports_federation_result_control \\\n  --stop-after-init\ndocker compose restart odoo\n```\n\n**Prevention**: always run `upgrade_sports_federation.sh` (or `-u <module>`)\nafter pulling code that adds or changes stored computed fields. A missing\ncolumn never appears in `--test-enable` output but will crash the live form.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Standings Not Recomputing After Result Approval\n\n**Symptom**: A result is approved (`result_state = approved`,\n`include_in_official_standings = True`) but the standings table is unchanged.\n\n**Cause A**: The standings record for the affected tournament/stage/group is\nin `frozen` state. Frozen standings are never recomputed automatically.\n\n**Fix A**:\n\n1. Open **Federation → Standings** and locate the relevant standings record.\n2. Verify `state = frozen`.\n3. Click **Unfreeze** (requires Federation Manager group).\n4. Click **Recompute**.\n5. Verify the standings are correct, then re-freeze.\n\n**Cause B**: The `@api.depends` chain on the standings recompute trigger is\nmissing the field that changed.\n\n**Fix B**:\n\n1. Check which field on `federation.match` changed (e.g. `home_score`).\n2. Verify it appears in the `@api.depends` decorator on\n   `_trigger_recompute` or the equivalent compute method in\n   `sports_federation_standings/models/federation_standings.py`.\n3. If missing, add the field to the depends list and upgrade the module.\n\n**Cause C**: The automatic trigger code path was skipped because the result\nwas approved via a raw ORM write (`record.write({\"result_state\": \"approved\"})`)\ninstead of the `action_approve_result()` method. This can happen during\nbulk imports.\n\n**Fix C**: Trigger a manual recompute from the standings form.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Notifications Not Sending\n\n**Symptom**: Expected emails (result approval, roster confirmation, referee\nassignment) are not delivered.\n\n**Cause A**: SMTP server is not configured or is misconfigured.\n\n**Fix A**:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Email → Outgoing Mail Servers**.\n2. Verify the server entry exists and is active.\n3. Click **Test Connection**. If it fails, correct the host, port, and\n   credentials.\n4. Check `docker compose logs odoo | grep -i smtp` for connection errors.\n\n**Cause B**: `sports_federation_notifications` module is not installed.\n\n**Fix B**:\n```bash\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo \\\n  -i sports_federation_notifications --stop-after-init\n```\n\n**Cause C**: The notification dispatcher scheduled action is disabled.\n\n**Fix C**:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions**.\n2. Find the federation notification scan action.\n3. Click **Run Manually** to test, then re-enable if it was disabled.\n\n**Cause D**: The email ends up in the mail queue but is not sent because the\nqueue runner is not processing.\n\n**Fix D**:\n```bash\n# Force the mail queue to flush\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo \\\n  -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo \\\n  --load=base,mail --stop-after-init \\\n  -e \"self.env['mail.mail'].process_email_queue()\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Import Wizard Dry-Run Always Fails\n\n**Symptom**: Running a dry-run in **Federation → Import Tools → Import Wizard**\nraises a duplicate key or unique constraint error on every attempt, even for\na fresh payload.\n\n**Cause**: Stale rows in the staging table (`federation.import.staged.delivery`\nor the module-specific staging model) from a previous failed import still\noccupy the unique key slot.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Open **Federation → Import Tools → Inbound Deliveries**.\n2. Filter for `state = staged` deliveries from the failing batch.\n3. Archive or delete the stale staged rows.\n\nAlternatively, trigger the cleanup scheduled action:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions**.\n2. Run **Federation: GC Staged Deliveries** manually.\n\n**Prevention**: the GC scheduled action runs daily. If it is disabled (see §5),\nstale rows accumulate quickly.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Rate Limit Buckets Never Cleared\n\n**Symptom**: The `federation.request.rate.limit` table grows unboundedly.\nPublic API calls succeed less frequently than expected even from legitimate\ncallers whose rate-limit window has expired.\n\n**Cause**: The `Federation: GC Rate Limit Buckets` scheduled action is\ndisabled.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Open **Settings → Technical → Automation → Scheduled Actions**.\n2. Find **Federation: GC Rate Limit Buckets**.\n3. Set **Active** = True and **Interval** to 1 Hour (the default).\n4. Click **Run Manually** to clear the backlog immediately.\n\n**Verify** bucket cleanup is working:\n```bash\ndocker compose exec -T db psql -U odoo -d odoo \\\n  -c \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM federation_request_rate_limit;\"\n# Should decrease after the GC action runs\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. CI Container Fails to Start PostgreSQL\n\n**Symptom**: Running `bash addons/ci/run_tests.sh` fails immediately with\na PostgreSQL startup error: `address already in use` or `port 5432 already\nin use`.\n\n**Cause**: The development Docker Compose stack is already running and its\n`db` service occupies port 5432 (if the CI uses host networking) or the same\nDocker network.\n\n**Fix**:\n\n```bash\n# Option A: stop the dev stack before running CI\ndocker compose down\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Option B: use a different network (check ci/run_tests.sh --help for options)\nbash addons/ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core --network ci_net\n```\n\nAfter CI completes, restart the dev stack:\n```bash\ndocker compose up -d\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Portal Page Shows 403 / `AccessError`\n\n**Symptom**: A portal user navigates to a federation portal page and receives\na 403 error or an `AccessError` in the logs.\n\n**Cause A**: The user's `res.users` record is not linked to a\n`federation.club.representative` record for the club that owns the resource.\n\n**Fix A**:\n1. Open **Federation → Portal → Club Representatives**.\n2. Verify a record exists for the user and the correct club.\n3. If missing, create it (see [WORKFLOW_CLUB_ONBOARDING.md](\n   _workflows/WORKFLOW_CLUB_ONBOARDING.md)).\n\n**Cause B**: The portal record rule for the affected model uses the wrong\ndomain expression (developer error introduced by a recent change).\n\n**Fix B**:\n1. Check **Settings → Technical → Security → Record Rules** for rules on the\n   affected model.\n2. Verify the domain matches the expected club-scoping pattern\n   (`club_id.representative_ids.user_id`, etc.).\n\n---\n\n## 8. Public JSON Feed Returns `500`\n\n**Symptom**: `GET /competitions/api/json` returns HTTP 500 instead of JSON.\n\n**Cause A**: A new required computed field on `federation.tournament` throws\nan exception when the tournament has incomplete data.\n\n**Fix A**: Check the Odoo log for the traceback:\n```bash\ndocker compose logs odoo 2>&1 | grep -A 30 \"competitions/api/json\"\n```\nFix the underlying data or guard the computed field with a `try/except`.\n\n**Cause B**: The rate-limit table has a corrupt bucket (e.g. `hit_count < 0`).\n\n**Fix B**:\n```bash\ndocker compose exec -T db psql -U odoo -d odoo \\\n  -c \"DELETE FROM federation_request_rate_limit WHERE hit_count < 0;\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9. Player Shows `is_eligible = False` After License Activation\n\n**Symptom**: A license is set to `state = active` but the player's\n`is_eligible` computed field remains `False`.\n\n**Cause A**: Odoo's compute cache is stale. This can happen after a direct\ndatabase write (e.g. during a migration or import) that bypasses the ORM.\n\n**Fix A**:\n```bash\n# Force recompute of is_eligible for all players\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo shell -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo <<'EOF'\nenv['federation.player'].search([])._compute_is_eligible()\nenv.cr.commit()\nEOF\n```\n\n**Cause B**: The player also has an active suspension sanction in\n`sports_federation_discipline`. Suspension overrides the license-active state.\n\n**Fix B**: Check **Federation → Discipline → Sanctions** for an active\nsuspension for the player. If the suspension is resolved, run the\nreinstatement action (see [WORKFLOW_PLAYER_LICENSE.md](\n_workflows/WORKFLOW_PLAYER_LICENSE.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Finance Events Not Exporting to Partner\n\n**Symptom**: A partner calls `GET /integration/v1/finance-events` and\nreceives an empty list even though events exist in the system.\n\n**Cause A**: Events are still in `draft` state. The integration export endpoint\nreturns only `confirmed` or `exported` events.\n\n**Fix A**: Federation finance staff must confirm the pending events:\n**Federation → Finance → Finance Events → filter `state = draft` → Confirm**.\n\n**Cause B**: The partner's `X-Federation-Partner-Code` header does not match\nthe code stored on the `federation.integration.partner` record.\n\n**Fix B**: Verify the partner code with the administrator. The export route\nreturns `access_denied` (not an empty list) for authentication failures.\nIf the response is an empty list with status 200, the authentication succeeded\nbut no confirmed events match the filter.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Reporting Schedule Stuck in `running`\n\n**Symptom**: A report schedule shows `state = running` indefinitely; no report\nis generated and no error is visible.\n\n**Cause**: The Odoo worker that started the report generation crashed (e.g.\nOOM kill, container restart) mid-execution, leaving the state flag uncleared.\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Open **Federation → Reporting → Report Schedules**.\n2. Set the stuck schedule back to `draft` or `ready` via the developer mode\n   form editor, or use:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose exec odoo odoo shell -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo <<'EOF'\nenv['federation.report.schedule'].search([('state','=','running')])\\\n  .write({'state': 'ready'})\nenv.cr.commit()\nEOF\n```\n\n3. Trigger the schedule manually to confirm it completes.\n\n**Prevention**: monitor the **Reporting → Report Schedules** list after every\ncontainer restart.\n\n---\n\n## 12. Open the roster line form and check the **Readiness** tab.\n2. If feedback is empty, check the player's license state, suspension status,\n   and team/season scope manually.\n3. If this is a new condition that lacks feedback, add the missing feedback\n   string in `sports_federation_rosters/models/roster_line.py` →\n   `_compute_readiness_feedback`.\n\n---\n\n## Getting Further Help\n\nIf none of the above applies:\n\n1.  {"content": "# Workflow: Club Representative Appeal & Dispute\n\nEnd-to-end process for raising, reviewing, and resolving a result or standing\ndispute submitted by a club representative.\n\nThis workflow is intentionally a thin, requester-facing wrapper around\n`WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md`, which is the canonical exception engine.\nDo not duplicate full exception mechanics here; use this workflow to describe\nclub-entry and follow-up touchpoints only.\n\n## Overview\n\nWhen a club representative believes a match result is incorrect or that a ruling\nwas applied unfairly, they can raise a formal dispute. The dispute is captured as\na `federation.override_request` and goes through the governance review pipeline.\nThe outcome may be a result correction, a sanction reduction, a standing\nadjustment, or a formal rejection with reasons.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests, decisions, audit notes, outcomes |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result correction after approved override |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standing adjustment after result correction |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Club representative raises appeal via portal or back-office |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Notifications to all parties at key decision points |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core club / match records referenced by the request |\n| `mail` | Chatter audit trail on the override request |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.override.request` | `title`, `request_type`, `target_model`, `target_res_id`, `reason`, `state`, `requester_id`, `decision_note`, `implementation_note` |\n\n## Override Request Types relevant to appeals\n\n| Type | Use case |\n|------|---------|\n| `result_correction` | Incorrect score, forfeit dispute, missing goal |\n| `standing_adjustment` | Points awarded incorrectly; does not require score change |\n| `eligibility_waiver` | Player ruled ineligible unfairly |\n| `sanction_reduction` | Disciplinary fine or suspension reduction request |\n\n## State Machine\n\n```\ndraft → submitted → approved → implemented → closed\n                 ↘ rejected  → closed\n      ← withdrawn (submitted → draft)\n```\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Club Representative Raises a Dispute\n\n**Actor**: Club representative\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance` (via portal or back office)\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Governance → Override Requests** (back office) or\n   the portal appeal section (if enabled).\n2. Click **New** and fill in:\n   - **Title** — clear one-line description of the dispute\n   - **Request Type** — e.g. `result_correction`\n   - **Target Record** — the match, result, or standing being disputed (set\n     `target_model` and `target_res_id`)\n   - **Reason** — full factual justification\n3. Save in `draft` state. Add supporting attachments via the chatter.\n4. Click **Submit** when ready: `draft → submitted`.\n\nThe requester and request timestamp are recorded automatically.\n\n**Withdrawal**: if the club needs to amend the request before a decision is\nmade, click **Withdraw** to return from `submitted → draft`, edit, and resubmit.\n\n### 2. Federation Staff Governance Review\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. Open the submitted request from\n   **Federation → Governance → Override Requests → Submitted**.\n2. Review the request, target record, and any supporting attachments.\n3. Use the chatter to request clarification from the club if needed (keeps a\n   timestamped record).\n4. Add **Audit Notes** for internal commentary that should not be visible to\n   the club representative.\n\nThere is no separate `under_review` state. Operational review happens while the\nrequest remains in `submitted` state.\n\n### 3. Decision Recording\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\nAfter review, the governance officer decides:\n\n- **Approve**: `submitted → approved`\n  - Add a `decision_note` explaining the basis for approval.\n  - The standard approve action creates a decision record automatically.\n- **Reject**: `submitted → rejected`\n  - Add a `decision_note` with the rejection reason.\n  - The club representative is notified (if notifications module is installed).\n\nThe governance officer records only the decision — implementation is handled\nseparately to keep the audit trail clean.\n\n### 4. Decision Notification\n\n**Actor**: System\n**Module**: `sports_federation_notifications`\n\nOn state transition to `approved` or `rejected`:\n\n- The club representative (requester) receives a notification with the decision\n  and the `decision_note`.\n- The federation manager group receives a notification for `approved` requests\n  that require implementation.\n\n### 5. Outcome Implementation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance` + affected owning module\n\nIf approved:\n\n| Request Type | Implementation Action |\n|---|---|\n| `result_correction` | Update `home_score` / `away_score` on the match; re-run result approval pipeline |\n| `standing_adjustment` | Unfreeze standings if frozen; manually adjust; re-freeze |\n| `eligibility_waiver` | Create or reinstate player license; update roster line |\n| `sanction_reduction` | Edit disciplinary sanction amount or suspension length |\n\nSteps:\n1. Open the approved override request.\n2. Implement the correction in the relevant module (see table above).\n3. Record what was done in `implementation_note` on the request form.\n4. Click **Mark Implemented**: `approved → implemented`.\n5. An outcome-log row is written automatically so later review can see what was\n   done, not just what was approved.\n\n### 6. Closure\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer or federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\nOnce all follow-up is complete:\n\n1. Open the `implemented` or `rejected` request.\n2. Click **Close**: state → `closed`.\n3. Only `implemented` or `rejected` requests can be closed.\n4. Closed requests are read-only and permanently preserved in the audit trail.\n\n## Audit Trail\n\nThe complete audit trail includes:\n\n- Request creation with requester and timestamp\n- Submission and any withdrawal back to draft (with timestamps)\n- Decision (approve / reject) with decision note and officer identity\n- Implementation note describing what was done\n- Closure timestamp\n\nAll state transitions are logged in the chatter via `mail.tracking.value`.\n\n## Impact on Standings\n\nFor result corrections that change scores:\n\n1. Corrected result re-enters the approval pipeline: the administrator re-submits\n   and re-approves the result.\n2. Standings in `draft` or `ready` state recompute automatically.\n3. If standings are `frozen`, the administrator must unfreeze → recompute →\n   re-freeze (see [WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md](WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md)).\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md](WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md) — Generic override request process for all exception types.\n- [WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — Result approval and re-approval after correction.\n- [WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md](WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md) — Freeze / unfreeze and recompute steps.\n\nUnified operator model reminder:\n\n- Raise dispute/request exception on the owning record.\n- Resolve through Governance Override.\n- Re-run result approval and standings publication recovery where needed.\n", "content_length": 7409, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "063f3e885e799adca4fdff955d7222fbc4332d02038b775bc52176ca5601c251", "size_bytes": 7467}
 {"content": "# Workflow: Club Onboarding\n\nEnd-to-end process for registering a new club with the federation — from initial\nrequest through compliance document intake, bank-details entry, first-season\nregistration, and portal access grant.\n\n## Overview\n\nA new club must be formally onboarded before it can enter teams in tournaments.\nOnboarding spans four areas: master-data setup, compliance document collection,\nfinance details, and portal access for the club representative. New Club Request\n\n**Actor**: Club applicant (off-system) → Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base`\n\nThe federation receives a new-club application through its standard intake\nchannel (email, paper form, or future portal form). Fill in:\n   - **Name** — official club name\n   - **Code** — short unique code (e.g. `MFC`)\n   - **Email**, **Phone**, **Website** (optional)\n   - **Address** — postal address for correspondence\n3. Save. The club starts with `active = True` and no additional state.\n\nAt this point the club exists in the system but is not yet enrolled in any season\nand has no compliance documents or portal access.\n\n### 2. Federation Staff Review\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base` + `sports_federation_compliance`\n\nBefore proceeding with compliance intake, the administrator performs a background\nreview:\n\n- Verify the club is not a duplicate (search by name and code).\n- Confirm the founding documents meet federation bylaws.\n- Confirm at least one responsible contact person has been nominated.\n\nNo formal review state exists on the club record itself. Use the chatter\n(Discuss tab on the club form) to record review notes.\n\n### 3. Compliance Document Intake\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator or club contact\n**Module**: `sports_federation_compliance`\n\nCreate one `federation.compliance.submission` per document requirement that\napplies to clubs (`required_for_all = True` for the `club` target model):\n\nCommon requirements at onboarding:\n\n| Requirement | Expiry? | Notes |\n|------------|---------|-------|\n| Public Liability Insurance | Yes (annual) | Minimum coverage amount per federation rules |\n| Club Registration Certificate | No | Official registration with national authority |\n| Bank Account Confirmation Letter | No | Matches bank details to be entered |\n| Club Rules & Constitution | No | Signed copy |\n\nFor each document:\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Compliance → Document Submissions**.\n2. Create a submission linked to the club and the relevant requirement.\n3. Attach the scanned or PDF document.\n4. Submit: state `draft → submitted`.\n5. The compliance officer reviews and approves: state `submitted → approved`.\n\nIf `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, an approval confirmation is\nsent to the club contact on each approval.\n\n### 4. Bank Details Entry\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_finance_bridge`\n\n1. On the club form, open the **Finance** tab (added by `sports_federation_finance_bridge`).\n2. Enter bank account details (IBAN, bank name, account holder name).\n3. These details are used when generating registration-fee finance events for\n   accounting integration exports.\n\n### 5. First Season Registration\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator or club representative\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base` + `sports_federation_portal`\n\nOnce compliance documents are approved, the club can register for the current\nseason:\n\n**Via back-office**:\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Registrations → Season Registrations**.\n2. Create a registration record for the club's first team in the current season.\n3. State: `draft → submitted → confirmed`.\n\n**Via portal (if portal module is installed)**:\n\n1. Club representative logs into the portal.\n2. Navigates to the Season Registrations section.\n3. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}
 {"content": "# ADR-0003: Public Route Ownership\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPublic tournament pages, feeds, calendars, registration entry points, and compatibility aliases can collide when several addons define overlapping controllers. Numeric legacy routes also create ambiguity about the canonical public contract.\n\n## Decision\n\n- `/competitions` and `/competitions/<edition-slug>` are the canonical public page routes.\n- Tournament-named page routes are compatibility redirects only.\n\nPublic route ownership is tournament-first and module-explicit:\n\n- `sports_federation_public_site` owns canonical public competition pages and match-day publication views; legacy tournament feeds and calendars remain compatibility contracts.\n- Slug-first routes are canonical for new consumers.\n- Numeric and competition-named routes may remain only as documented compatibility aliases with an owner and review date.\n- Public reads enforce applicable publication controls such as `website_published`, `show_public_results`, and `show_public_standings`.\n- Public write entry points use a model-owned request boundary and must not broaden portal or backend privileges.\n- Route inventory, OpenAPI contracts, compatibility notes, and smoke coverage are part of the ownership boundary.\n- Duplicate or shadow public controllers are removed rather than kept as silent fallbacks.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Controller precedence and deprecation become reviewable.\n- New public surfaces must update route and contract documentation in the same change.\n- Compatibility routes carry an explicit maintenance cost and sunset decision.\n- Publication defaults remain deny-by-default.\n", "content_length": 1753, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0003-public-route-ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "8f2952d166f7cf414b532edcbbe59159565833ea88c150bdc2b4a5248d639a7d", "size_bytes": 1753}

 {"content": "# Competition Workflow in the User Interface\n\nOwner: Federation Competition Operations\nLast verified against menu XML: 2026-09-04\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis guide replaces conceptual module names with the menus that actually exist in the **Federation** application. Prepare reusable setup\n\nUse:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Seasons\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Templates\nFederation > Competitions > Rules & Policies > Rule Sets & Policies\nFederation > Clubs & People > Club Directory > Clubs\nFederation > Clubs & People > Club Directory > Teams\n```\n\nCreate the season, reusable competition definition, rule set, clubs, and teams. Points, tie-break, eligibility, and qualification components are below **Rules & Policies > Advanced Components**.\n\n**Recovery:** Edit unused records. Archive records that already have history. Do not delete referenced seasons, competitions, clubs, teams, or rule sets merely to restart a workflow.\n\n### 2. Create the season competition\n\nPreferred menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Create Competition\n```\n\nThe wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.\n\nInspect the records through:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Season Competitions\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Records > Structure & Fixtures > Divisions & Tournaments\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Competition Overview\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.\n\n### 3. Open registration and accept entries\n\nBackend:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Season registrations\n```\n\nUse **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.\n\n**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.\n\n### 4. Finalize participants\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClose the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.\n\n### 5. Configure and generate the format\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Format Templates\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Format Studio\n```\n\n**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.\n\n**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.\n\n### 6. Prepare and progress stages\n\nThere is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Format Studio\n```\n\nAvailable stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.\n\n### 7. Plan calendar capacity\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Calendar Planner\n```\n\nCreate match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Operations > Venues\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.\n\n### 8. Build the working schedule\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.\n\n**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.\n\n### 9. Submit and review the schedule\n\nPlanner menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Schedule Review Queue\n```\n\nThe review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.\n\n**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.\n\n### 10. Publish the schedule\n\nUse **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publishing > Approved Schedules\nFederation > Publishing > Schedule Publications\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.\n\n### 11. Operate match day\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Match-Day Control\n```\n\nUse **Open Match Day** when ready. During operations use **Update Court**, **Report Incident**, or **Operational Schedule Change**. Finish with **Close Match Day**. Supporting records are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Operations > Match Sheets\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Technical Records > Incidents\nFederation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Technical Records > Operational Deviations\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Resolve incident and deviation records with **Resolve**. Operational changes are recorded rather than silently altering the approved publication. Correct the planning baseline through a schedule amendment.\n\n### 12. Submit and approve results\n\nBackend menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Operations > Matches\n```\n\nResult Control extends the match form; there is no separate backend **Results** menu. The form provides **Submit Result**, **Verify Result**, **Approve Result**, **Raise Dispute / Request Exception**, **Correct Result**, and **Reset to Draft**.\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Results\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Reset an incorrect in-progress result to draft. Raise a dispute for governed review. Correct contested or approved results through **Correct Result**. Never silently edit an approved score.\n\n### 13. Recompute and freeze standings\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publishing > Standings\n```\n\nUse **Recompute** or **Queue Recompute**, inspect lines and tie-break notes, and then use **Freeze**.\n\n**Recovery:** Recompute while unfrozen. For a frozen standing, use **Unfreeze**, correct the source result or rule, use **Force Recompute**, and freeze again. Failed asynchronous work appears under the nested **Recompute Queue**.\n\n### 14. Monitor exceptions\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Administration > Action Queue\nFederation > Insights > Reports & Insights > Overview & Readiness > Operational Health\nFederation > Administration > System Health > Operational Job Health\n```\n\nUse source links to correct business records in their owning workflow. Reparenting a menu must not broaden its groups or model access.\n- Empty compatibility categories are not retained.  {"content": "# Exception Handling Policy\n\nCatch expected domain failures narrowly (`ValidationError`, `AccessError`, `UserError`). Integration boundaries may catch `Exception` only when they log with correlation context, classify the failure, persist operator feedback, and do not report success. Silent `except Exception: pass` is prohibited. Cron batches isolate individual records but retain error evidence. +#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Apply selected integration environment variables into Odoo's
+# ir.config_parameter using the `odoo shell` inside the CI Odoo image.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   bash ci/apply_env_to_ir_config.sh <project_name> <compose_file> <env_file> <odoo_conf>
+#
+PROJECT_NAME="${1:-sf_ci}"
+COMPOSE_FILE="${2:-ci/docker-compose.ci.yaml}"
+LOADED_ENV_FILE="${3:-ci/.env}"
+GENERATED_CONF="${4:-ci/odoo-ci.generated.runtime.conf}"
+CONTAINER_CONF="/etc/odoo/odoo.conf"
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+
+if [[ -f "$LOADED_ENV_FILE" ]]; then
+  set -a
+  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
+  source "$LOADED_ENV_FILE"
+  set +a
+fi
+
+# Keep credentials consistent with run_tests.sh when the checked-out env file
+# uses CRLF line endings.
+CI_POSTGRES_USER="${CI_POSTGRES_USER//$'\r'/}"
+CI_POSTGRES_PASSWORD="${CI_POSTGRES_PASSWORD//$'\r'/}"
+CI_POSTGRES_DB="${CI_POSTGRES_DB//$'\r'/}"
+CI_ODOO_DB_HOST="${CI_ODOO_DB_HOST//$'\r'/}"
+CI_ODOO_DB_PORT="${CI_ODOO_DB_PORT//$'\r'/}"
+export CI_POSTGRES_USER CI_POSTGRES_PASSWORD CI_POSTGRES_DB \
+  CI_ODOO_DB_HOST CI_ODOO_DB_PORT
+
+echo "[CI] Applying integration envs to Odoo ir.config_parameter (if any)" >&2
+
+docker compose -p "$PROJECT_NAME" -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" run --rm ci-odoo \
+  sh -lc 'if command -v gosu >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec gosu odoo odoo shell -c "$1"; elif command -v runuser >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec runuser -u odoo -- odoo shell -c "$1"; else echo "ERROR: cannot drop root privileges before starting Odoo" >&2; exit 2; fi' \
+  sh "$CONTAINER_CONF" <<'PY'
+import os
+
+keys = [
+    "SMTP_HOST", "SMTP_PORT", "SMTP_USER", "SMTP_PASSWORD", "SMTP_USE_TLS", "EMAIL_FROM",
+    "SENDGRID_API_KEY", "MAILGUN_API_KEY",
+    "OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID", "OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET", "OAUTH_GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI",
+    "OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID", "OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET", "OAUTH_GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI",
+    "TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID", "TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN",
+    "SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL",
+    "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "S3_BUCKET", "S3_REGION", "ALLOWED_HOSTS",
+]
+
+for k in keys:
+    v = os.environ.get(k)
+    if v:
+        keyname = 'integration.' + k.lower()
+        env['ir.config_parameter'].set_param(keyname, v)
+        print('SET', keyname)
+PY
+
+echo "[CI] apply_env_to_ir_config.sh completed" >&2
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Create a deterministic inventory of security and architecture hotspots.
+
+The inventory is evidence, not a policy gate. It gives reviewers one stable list
+of addons, routes, elevated calls, raw SQL, scheduled jobs, migrations, and large
+Python files for the exact candidate being qualified.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import ast
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+DEFAULT_LARGE_FILE_LINES = 500
+ROUTE_RE = re.compile(r"@(?:http\.)?route\s*\(")
+SUDO_RE = re.compile(r"\.sudo\s*\(")
+SQL_RE = re.compile(r"(?:\.execute\s*\(|\b(?:SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|ALTER|CREATE|DROP)\b)", re.I)
+CRON_RE = re.compile(r"<record\b[^>]*\bmodel=[\"']ir\.cron[\"']", re.I)
+MODEL_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*_(?:name|inherit)\s*=\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']", re.M)
+
+
+def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", *args], cwd=repo, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True
+    )
+    return result.stdout.strip()
+
+
+def discover_addons(repo: Path) -> list[Path]:
+    return sorted(
+        path.parent
+        for path in repo.glob("sports_federation_*/__manifest__.py")
+        if path.is_file()
+    )
+
+
+def parse_manifest(path: Path) -> dict:
+    try:
+        value = ast.literal_eval(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except (SyntaxError, ValueError) as exc:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Invalid manifest {path}: {exc}") from exc
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise SystemExit(f"Manifest is not a dictionary: {path}")
+    return value
+
+
+def location(repo: Path, path: Path, lineno: int, text: str = "") -> dict:
+    item = {"path": path.relative_to(repo).as_posix(), "line": lineno}
+    if text:
+        item["text"] = text.strip()[:240]
+    return item
+
+
+def scan_python(repo: Path, path: Path, large_file_lines: int, result: dict) -> None:
+    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+    lines = text.splitlines()
+    if len(lines) >= large_file_lines:
+        result["large_python_files"].append(
+            {**location(repo, path, 1), "lines": len(lines)}
+        )
+    for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+        if SUDO_RE.search(line):
+            result["sudo_calls"].append(location(repo, path, lineno, line))
+        if SQL_RE.search(line) and not line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            result["raw_sql_candidates"].append(location(repo, path, lineno, line))
+        if ROUTE_RE.search(line):
+            block = " ".join(lines[lineno - 1 : min(lineno + 9, len(lines))])
+            result["routes"].append(
+                {
+                    **location(repo, path, lineno, line),
+                    "auth": _keyword(block, "auth"),
+                    "csrf": _keyword(block, "csrf"),
+                    "methods": _keyword(block, "methods"),
+                }
+            )
+    for model in MODEL_NAME_RE.findall(text):
+        result["model_declarations"].append(
+            {"path": path.relative_to(repo).as_posix(), "model": model}
+        )
+
+
+def _keyword(block: str, name: str):
+    match = re.search(rf"\b{name}\s*=\s*([^,\)]+)", block)
+    return match.group(1).strip() if match else None
+

+def build_inventory(repo: Path, large_file_lines: int) -> dict:
+    addons = discover_addons(repo)
+    result = {
+        "schema_version": 1,
+        "commit": git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"),
+        "addons": [],
+        "routes": [],
+        "sudo_calls": [],
+        "raw_sql_candidates": [],
+        "scheduled_jobs": [],
+        "migrations": [],
+        "model_declarations": [],
+        "large_python_files": [],
+    }
+    for addon in addons:
+        manifest = parse_manifest(addon / "__manifest__.py")
+        result["addons"].append(
+            {
+                "name": addon.name,
+                "version": manifest.get("version"),
+                "depends": sorted(manifest.get("depends", [])),
+                "installable": bool(manifest.get("installable", True)),
+            }
+        )
+    roots = addons + [repo / "ci", repo / "scripts"]
+    files = sorted(
+        {path for root in roots if root.exists() for path in root.rglob("*") if path.is_file()}
+    )
+    for path in files:
+        rel = path.relative_to(repo).as_posix()
+        if path.suffix == ".py":
+            scan_python(repo, path, large_file_lines, result)
+        elif path.suffix == ".xml":
+            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+            for match in CRON_RE.finditer(text):
+                result["scheduled_jobs"].append(
+                    location(repo, path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+        if "/migrations/" in f"/{rel}" and path.suffix in {".py", ".sql"}:
+            result["migrations"].append(rel)
+    for key in (
+        "routes", "sudo_calls", "raw_sql_candidates", "scheduled_jobs",
+        "model_declarations", "large_python_files",
+    ):
+        result[key] = sorted(result[key], key=lambda item: (item["path"], item.get("line", 0), item.get("model", "")))
+    result["migrations"].sort()
+    canonical = json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+    result["inventory_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(canonical).hexdigest()
+    result["counts"] = {
+        "addons": len(result["addons"]),
+        "routes": len(result["routes"]),
+        "sudo_calls": len(result["sudo_calls"]),
+        "raw_sql_candidates": len(result["raw_sql_candidates"]),
+        "scheduled_jobs": len(result["scheduled_jobs"]),
+        "migrations": len(result["migrations"]),
+        "model_declarations": len(result["model_declarations"]),
+        "large_python_files": len(result["large_python_files"]),
+    }
+    return result

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Validate a complete release evidence set and write its summary manifest."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import subprocess
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+DEFAULT_REQUIRED_LANES = (
+    "preflight",
+    "static",
+    "install",
+    "upgrade",
+    "core",
+    "portal",
+    "public",
+    "performance",
+    "acceptance",
+    "focus",
+    "full",
+)
+
+
+def current_commit(root: Path) -> str:
+    return subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
+        cwd=root,
+        check=True,
+        text=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+    ).stdout.strip()
+
+
+def load_lane_records(evidence_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
+    records = {}
+    for path in sorted(evidence_dir.glob("lane-*.json")):
+        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        lane = record.get("lane")
+        if not lane:
+            raise ValueError(f"Evidence has no lane: {path}")
+        if lane in records:
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate evidence for lane: {lane}")
+        records[lane] = record
+    return records
+
+
+
+def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def log_is_valid(record: dict) -> bool:
+    log = record.get("log", {})
+    path_value = log.get("path")
+    if not path_value or not log.get("sha256"):
+        return False
+    path = Path(path_value)
+    return (
+        path.is_file()
+        and path.stat().st_size == log.get("size_bytes")
+        and sha256(path) == log.get("sha256")
+    )
+
+
+def build_summary(
+    evidence_dir: Path,
+    required_lanes: tuple[str, ...],
+    expected_commit: str,
+) -> dict:
+    records = load_lane_records(evidence_dir)
+    missing = sorted(set(required_lanes) - set(records))
+    unexpected = sorted(set(records) - set(required_lanes))
+    commit_mismatches = sorted(
+        lane
+        for lane, record in records.items()
+        if record.get("commit") != expected_commit
+    )
+    invalid_records = sorted(
+        lane
+        for lane, record in records.items()
+        if record.get("schema_version") != 2
+        or record.get("status") not in {"passed", "failed", "skipped"}
+        or record.get("exit_code") is None
+        or not record.get("command")
+        or not record.get("started_at")
+        or not record.get("finished_at")
+        or record.get("duration_seconds") is None
+        or not log_is_valid(record)
+        or (
+            record.get("status") == "failed"
+            and not record.get("failure_classification")
+        )
+        or (record.get("status") == "skipped" and not record.get("skip_reason"))
+    )
+    failed = sorted(
+        lane for lane, record in records.items() if record.get("status") == "failed"
+    )
+    skipped = sorted(
+        lane for lane, record in records.items() if record.get("status") == "skipped"
+    )
+    passed = sorted(
+        lane for lane, record in records.items() if record.get("status") == "passed"
+    )
+    complete = (
+        not missing
+        and not unexpected
+        and not commit_mismatches
+        and not invalid_records
+    )
+    status = "passed" if complete and not failed and not skipped else "failed"
+    return {
+        "schema_version": 2,
+        "recorded_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+        "commit": expected_commit,
+        "status": status,
+        "complete": complete,
+        "required_lanes": list(required_lanes),
+        "passed_lanes": passed,
+        "failed_lanes": failed,
+        "skipped_lanes": skipped,
+        "missing_lanes": missing,
+        "unexpected_lanes": unexpected,
+        "commit_mismatches": commit_mismatches,
+        "invalid_records": invalid_records,
+        "lanes": [records[lane] for lane in sorted(records)],
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--evidence-dir", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, default=Path.cwd())
+    parser.add_argument("--required-lane", action="append", dest="required_lanes")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    required_lanes = tuple(args.required_lanes or DEFAULT_REQUIRED_LANES)
+    output = args.output or args.evidence_dir / "summary.json"
+    summary = build_summary(
+        args.evidence_dir,
+        required_lanes,
+        current_commit(args.repo.resolve()),
+    )
+    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    output.write_text(
+        json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+    print(output)
+    return 0 if summary["status"] == "passed" else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
+

+All Odoo release lanes run inside the pinned `odoo:19` Docker image with the
+canonical Compose file `ci/docker-compose.ci.yaml`. The baseline retains one
+isolated Compose project while it runs the fresh-install, focused, and upgrade
+lanes, then removes the project after evidence capture. No host `odoo-bin`
+checkout is required.
+
+
+## Evidence completeness
+
+The baseline runs every required lane and records one `lane-<name>.json` file and
+one immutable log digest per lane. Required lanes are:
+
+- preflight;
+- static validation;
+- fresh install;
+- same-version upgrade;
+- competition core;
+- portal;
+- public site;
+- performance;
+- operator acceptance;
+- release focus;
+- full standard suite.
+
+A lane record contains the candidate SHA, exact command, start and finish time,
+duration, exit code, tool versions, runner identity, database name, and log hash.
+Failed lanes require a failure classification. The runner initially records
+`unclassified` unless the operator supplies a lane-specific environment value,
+for example:
+
+```bash
+export RELEASE_FAILURE_CLASSIFICATION_UPGRADE=migration_defect
+```
+
+Allowed classifications are defined by `ci/capture_release_evidence.py`. An
+unclassified failure remains a failed qualification and must be triaged before
+release approval.
+
+`ci/finalize_release_evidence.py` rejects missing, duplicate, skipped, malformed,
+or cross-commit lane evidence. A release summary passes only when every required
+lane is present for the current commit and every lane passed. Inventory JSON is
+supporting evidence and is deliberately excluded from lane status calculation.
+

+      -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "CREATE DATABASE \"$database\" OWNER \"$ci_postgres_user\";"
+  fi
+}

+def latest_artifact_directories() -> list[Path]:
+    """Return the newest artifact run directory for each artifact category."""
+    if not ARTIFACT_ROOT.is_dir():
+        return []
+
+    selected: list[Path] = []
+    for category in sorted(
+        (path for path in ARTIFACT_ROOT.iterdir() if path.is_dir()),
+        key=lambda path: path.name,
+    ):
+        runs = [path for path in category.iterdir() if path.is_dir()]
+        if runs:
+            selected.append(
+                max(runs, key=lambda path: (path.stat().st_mtime, path.name))
+            )
+    return selected
+
+
+def collect_latest_artifacts() -> set[Path]:
+    """Collect direct category files and files from the newest run per category."""
+    files: set[Path] = set()
+    if not ARTIFACT_ROOT.is_dir():
+        return files
+
+    for category in ARTIFACT_ROOT.iterdir():
+        if not category.is_dir():
+            continue
+        files.update(
+            repository_relative(path)
+            for path in category.iterdir()
+            if is_supported_text_file(path)
+        )
+
+    for directory in latest_artifact_directories():
+        files.update(collect_directory(directory))
+    return files
+

+common=(--no-http --stop-after-init --without-demo=all --log-level=test)
+
+export CI_PROJECT_NAME="$compose_project"
+export CI_POSTGRES_USER="$ci_postgres_user"
+export CI_POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$ci_postgres_password"
+export CI_POSTGRES_DB="$ci_postgres_db"
+export CI_ODOO_DB_HOST="$ci_odo_db_host"
+export CI_ODOO_DB_PORT="$ci_odo_db_port"
+export CI_ODOO_CONFIG_PATH="$config_path"
+
+validate_database_name() {
+  local database="$1"
+  if [[ ! "$database" =~ ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
+    echo "ERROR: invalid PostgreSQL database name: $database" >&2
+    exit 2
+  fi
+}
+
+require_compose() {
+  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
+    echo "ERROR: Docker is required for Odoo RC validation." >&2
+    exit 2
+  }
+  docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
+    echo "ERROR: Docker Compose is required for Odoo RC validation." >&2
+    exit 2
+  }
+}
+
+write_config() {
+  if [[ ! -f "$config_path" ]]; then
+    cat > "$config_path" <<EOF
+[options]
+db_host = $ci_odo_db_host
+db_port = $ci_odo_db_port
+db_user = $ci_postgres_user
+db_password = $ci_postgres_password
+addons_path = /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/odoo/addons,/mnt/extra-addons
+data_dir = /var/lib/odoo
+list_db = False
+http_interface = 127.0.0.1
+without_demo = True
+log_level = info
+EOF
+    chmod 0644 "$config_path"
+  fi
+}
+
+ensure_stack() {
+  require_compose
+  write_config
+  "${compose[@]}" up -d --wait ci-db
+  "${compose[@]}" exec -T \
+    -e PGPASSWORD="$ci_postgres_password" \
+    ci-db psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U "$ci_postgres_user" -d "$ci_postgres_db" \
+    -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "SELECT 1" >/dev/null
+}
+
+ensure_database() {
+  local database="$1"
+  validate_database_name "$database"
+  ensure_stack
+  if ! "${compose[@]}" exec -T ci-db \
+    psql -U "$ci_postgres_user" -d "$ci_postgres_db" -Atc \
+    "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$database'" | grep -q '^1$'; then
+    "${compose[@]}" exec -T ci-db \
+      psql -U "$ci_postgres_user" -d "$ci_postgres_db" \
+      -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "CREATE DATABASE \"$database\" OWNER \"$ci_postgres_user\";"
+  fi
+}
+
+cleanup_compose() {
+  require_compose
+  "${compose[@]}" down -v --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  rm -f "$config_path"
+}
+
+if [[ "${RC_COMPOSE_RETAIN:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
+  trap cleanup_compose EXIT
+fi

+def latest_artifact_directories() -> list[Path]:
+    """Return the newest artifact run directory for each artifact category."""
+    if not ARTIFACT_ROOT.is_dir():
+        return []
+
+    selected: list[Path] = []
+    for category in sorted(
+        (path for path in ARTIFACT_ROOT.iterdir() if path.is_dir()),
+        key=lambda path: path.name,
+    ):
+        runs = [path for path in category.iterdir() if path.is_dir()]
+        if runs:
+            selected.append(
+                max(runs, key=lambda path: (path.stat().st_mtime, path.name))
+            )
+    return selected
+
+
+def collect_latest_artifacts() -> set[Path]:
+    """Collect direct category files and files from the newest run per category."""
+    files: set[Path] = set()
+    if not ARTIFACT_ROOT.is_dir():
+        return files
+
+    for category in ARTIFACT_ROOT.iterdir():
+        if not category.is_dir():
+            continue
+        files.update(
+            repository_relative(path)
+            for path in category.iterdir()
+            if is_supported_text_file(path)
+        )
+
+    for directory in latest_artifact_directories():
+        files.update(collect_directory(directory))
+    return files
+
